title: Biltmore Championship Asheville shines on day 2 of golf tournament
description: On Sept. 18, 2026, Western North Carolina residents and tourists rooted for the golfers in the inaugural Biltmore Championship Asheville.
fullText:
ASHEVILLE - On Sept. 18, the Blue Ridge Mountains framed the PGA Tour's Biltmore Championship Asheville, which is in full swing from Sept. 17-20 at The Cliffs at Walnut Cove in Arden.

Off the green, the audience politely applauded the players in the tournament that began with nearly 130 competitors.

For many, it was their first time seeing a PGA Tour event live.

Griffin Collins, an Atlanta resident, said he had attended PGA Tour events before that and said the Biltmore Championship Asheville stands up to the best of them.

"It's super cool. The course is beautiful," he said.

Collins attended the Biltmore Championship Asheville with friends the day before his wedding in the city. It was a bonus for the golf fan, as the wedding was planned before the PGA Tour announced.

It's the first PGA Tour event in Asheville in 84 years, hosted on the Jack Nicklaus-designed course at a venue more than 23,000 square feet, which opened in 2005.

"It is a beautiful day to showcase Asheville and Western North Carolina to the entire golfing world," Governor Josh Stein said on the second morning of the tournament. "It's going to show these gorgeous mountains to viewers all over the world, and people are going to say to themselves, 'I want to go there,' and that's what we want to do ― let the world know Western North Carolina is open for business."

Without a fog delay, as on the first day of the prestigious tournament, the professional men's golfers began the second day of the inaugural tournament under clear skies and sunshine, playing their way around the course and moving closer to claiming the victory, the custom-made gold-and-silver trophy and a cut of the $5 million purse.

The Biltmore Championship Asheville is the first of eight in the FedEx Fall Series, played after the Tour Championship, which finalizes eligibility for the 2027 PGA Tour Season.

Collins was rooting for the Vanderbilt University alum Gordon Sargent.

"Hopefully he can get back in the league and get back up there," he said.

Before Stein made his rounds of the holes, he paused to comment on the players with local ties.

"It's great that some of the most talented golfers in the world are North Carolinians. We have J.T. Polston and Webb Simpson competing here, and we're cheering hard for them," he said.

The Biltmore Championship Asheville was secured through a $2.4 million four-year agreement between the PGA Tour and co-sponsors Biltmore, of the famed Biltmore Estate and Biltmore House, and Explore Asheville.

More than 10,000 guests were expected to attend the sold-out four-day event, with more than 2,000 out-of-state visitors, according to Explore Asheville. More than 1,100 volunteers registered to help before and during the tournament.

Anna Catherine, a Hickory resident and staff member at the University of North Carolina Asheville, signed up to volunteer three days over the weekend.

"It's a great way to get out and meet people and give back, which is one of the core pillars of what we do for the community, and I wanted to do my part," she said. "I wanted to be part of what makes it special and bringing people back to Asheville."

Stein said the PGA Tour is expected to significantly boost the region's economy, generating millions of dollars over the four-day weekend, accelerating WNC's recovery progress since Hurricane Helene, which arrived as a tropical storm in the fall of 2024.

Collins said he and his fiancée had visited Asheville many times before and after Helene, ultimately choosing an undisclosed venue in the city to exchange vows and celebrate.

"Our venue was under five feet of water but they rebuilt everything, so we felt good with going there since they were back up and running," he said.

During the four-day visit, he, his wedding party, and guests planned to venture outside The Cliffs at Walnut Cove to local businesses, including a welcome party at Hi-Wire Brewing, with food catered by Bear's Smokehouse BBQ, also a PGA Tour food vendor.

Collins said he planned to return for the next years of the Biltmore Championship Asheville.

Stein said the Biltmore Championship Asheville aims to accelerate the region's recovery, adding that there have been "encouraging indicators" of taxable sales in 2026, compared to before the historic storm.

"We see progress being made, but we know there's a lot more work to do," Stein said.

He said employment in Buncombe County hadn't fully rebounded, but that the way to boost employment is to increase local money circulation.

Asheville's unemployment rate was 3.3% in July 2026, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.

"We want the world to know what we know about Western North Carolina. It's so beautiful; the people are nice, they're friendly, they're kind. The food is great, the beer is good, the crafts are beautiful. There's just so much to enjoy in Western North Carolina; we want more people to come here and spend their money."

Tiana Kennell is the food and dining reporter for the Asheville Citizen Times, part of USA TODAY Co., covering the food and beverage industry and PGA Tour's Biltmore Championship Asheville. Tips, comments, questions? Email tkennell@citizentimes.com or follow @PrincessOfPage on Instagram.

title: Cowboys post questionable image of Commanders QB Jayden Daniels before deleting it
description: The Cowboys posted some images of their most recent home game against the Commanders. It featured
fullText:
In preparation for their Week 2 game against the Washington Commanders at AT&T Stadium, the Dallas Cowboys posted a collection of images from their matchups against Washington on X (formerly Twitter). One photo showed Dallas linebacker Shemar James celebrating after sacking Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels.

No problem, right? Of course not. Sacks are celebrated and should be celebrated. However, Daniels was lying on the ground, injured, and would leave the game after that play. He missed the rest of that Week 7 matchup; he returned two weeks later.

The Cowboys' social media team drew plenty of criticism for posting that specific image. Later on Friday, they deleted the entire post. But, as we know, the internet lives forever. Here's what the Dallas social media team posted.

It probably doesn't help that the image shows an injured Daniels on the ground in pain, with the caption, "some of our favorite moments vs. the Commanders." Considering that is one of their favorite moments against, they clearly don't appreciate the history between these two franchises dating back to 1960.

Were the Cowboys wrong for posting that specific image? It depends on who you ask. Remember, Jerry Jones, Brian Schottenheimer, and Dak Prescott weren't behind that. However, not every Dallas fan agreed with the post.

This is not a GOOD look from the #DallasCowboys social media team posting a still shot of a play that the other teams QB was injured.#DeleteThis https://t.co/cJ3A1Lt9rG pic.twitter.com/QXB1FVhzQO

Washington players aren't thinking about this. It wouldn't be surprising if a Commanders coach posted an image of the tweet in the locker room sometime ahead of Sunday's game, though. Why? Well, that's what coaches do. Always looking for an edge, even for something as simple as a social media post that none of the coaches or players had anything to do with.

Sunday's game is an important one for the Commanders and Cowboys. The loser of this game falls to 0-2, more importantly, 0-2 in the division.

title: Tennessee Titans vs. Philadelphia Eagles: 6 keys to victory in Week 2
description: There are six keys to victory for the Tennessee Titans against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2.
fullText:
The Tennessee Titans host the Philadelphia Eagles at Nissan Stadium in Nashville, Tennessee, at 12:00 p.m. CST this Sunday.

The Eagles beat the Washington Commanders by the skin of their teeth in Week 1, while the Titans fell to the Jets in a bad way.

These two teams are on very different levels right now. The Eagles have been at the top of the NFC East for the last several years (or second), and the Titans have been at the bottom of the AFC South for the last few years. Cam Ward gave this team hope. Robert Saleh boosted that hope. Then they fell. To the Jets. Now everyone is scratching their heads, wondering what happened.

The Titans are desperate to at least look like a decent football team against the Eagles on Sunday, while the Eagles are looking to sit atop the NFC East again. It's going to be a difficult day for Tennessee, but nothing is impossible.

Here are six keys to victory for the Titans against the Eagles in Week 2.

This has to be the Titans' top priority against the Eagles. Cam Ward took three sacks against the Jets and spent much of the game running for his life. He threw for just 140 yards and one touchdown against New York, and the Titans need more offensive production than that against the Eagles this week.

Ward doesn't need to throw the ball on every play. He needs defined reads, movement throws, and opportunities to use his legs while keeping the Eagles from teeing off on obvious passing downs. Jalen Carter is going to be a problem for the Titans' offensive line, but they have to find a way to limit his penetration.

This isn't just about containment. Tennessee has to prevent the Eagles from turning designed runs and scrambles into easy explosives. Force Hurts to consistently make throws from the pocket and live with the results.

This is where Jeffery Simmons comes in. The biggest individual battle in this game is Simmons versus the Eagles' interior. Simmons has to break through Hurts' protection, but if he's going to get to the quarterback, the rest of his line has to leave no room for Hurts to run.

Eagles guard Landon Dickerson landed on injured reserve, and Philadelphia is working through different possibilities at left guard. This is where Tennessee's defensive line needs to create chaos. They don't need to rack up a ton of sacks, but penetration, negative runs, and hurried decisions from Hurts will lead to mistakes.

If the offensive line does its job and Cam Ward can get the ball out, the Titans have to attack the Eagles' secondary with explosive plays. Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson each caught five or fewer passes for 38 yards in Week 1, so Tennessee needs more explosive production from its passing game.

Philadelphia's Cooper DeJean is also dealing with a calf/abdomen injury. He was limited Thursday after missing Wednesday's practice.

Tennessee has to attack downfield.

To get those explosive plays downfield, the Titans must establish the ground game early. They can't put the entire game on Cam Ward's right arm. Philadelphia's run defense ranked 22nd in the NFL last season, allowing 124.4 yards per game. Get Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears involved early. Force the Eagles to respect the ground game.

Even if Tennessee doesn't rip off huge runs, establishing the ground game can slow the Eagles' pass rush. This makes it easier to attack the secondary and keeps the offense on schedule.

Last week, the Titans converted 33.33% (4-of-12) of their third-down attempts. They only had 11 first downs in the entire game. The Jets converted on two of 12 third-down attempts, converted both fourth-down attempts, and managed 19 first downs overall.

Winning on third down is one of the most important keys to this game. Philadelphia's offense becomes extremely difficult to defend when it consistently stays ahead of the sticks. Tennessee needs to create second-and-long situations, get Philadelphia into third-and-7-plus, and then get off the field.

Offensively, they must find a way into third-and-short situations to give Ward an easier shot at moving the chains.

Can we find the end zone this week? Field goals won't get the job done against the Eagles; the Titans must find the end zone, especially if the Eagles' offense gets rolling.

How do they do that? Run the ball. Stay out of obvious passing situations. Protect Cam Ward. PROTECT CAM WARD. That's the biggest key to this game. Protecting him keeps the offense from becoming one-dimensional and gives the Titans a chance to move the ball down the field.

Defensively, they must pressure Jalen Hurts. Force Philadelphia to sustain drives and capitalize on opportunities. If Cedric Gray returns to the field, this will be an easier task. He practiced fully on Wednesday and Thursday, but his injury designation won't be revealed until they're sure. Last season's leading tackler was sorely missed against the Jets last week. Getting him back for this game will boost the defensive confidence and morale.

title: Former Texas A&M coach reportedly eyeing a return to Florida State
description: Former Texas A&M coach Jimbo Fisher is reportedly eyeing a return to Florida State amid coaching uncertainty.
fullText:
Before Mike Elko was officially hired as Texas A&M's head coach just weeks before the conclusion of the 2023 regular season, Jimbo Fisher was the king of College Station for nearly six full seasons, leading the Aggies to three consecutive bowl game appearances during his first three seasons; but after finishing 9-1 during the COVID-shortened 2020 season, Fisher's massive extension became a bad omen for the veteran head coach.

Finishing 5-7 during the 2022 season, months after landing the No. 1 2022 recruiting class, Fisher's future with the Aggies, despite his extension, was on thin ice, and after starting 6-4 in 2023, the board of regents made the tough financial decision to relieve Fisher of his duties a week before the regular-season finale vs. LSU.

Biting the bullet, the Aggies bought out Fisher's contract for a whopping $77.5 million, which they're still paying to this day, and while he has more than enough money to retire for good, Fisher's current stint as an ACC Network analyst may be a short-term gig.

According to Yahoo Sports and The Athletic, Florida State coach Mike Norvell's shaky future at the helm could lead to Jimbo Fisher returning as the program's head coach, a job he held for eight seasons after replacing legendary head coach Bobby Bowden, winning the 2013 national title and making the College Football Playoff once.

According to both sources, Fisher "really wants the job," and based on his recent comments about wanting to return to coaching, adjusting his outlook to the current chaotic college football landscape is vital if he has any legitimate shot at returning to the Power Four level.

title: School celebrates ex-pupil's international call-up
description: Kent-born Luis Binks has been named in Scotland's senior national football team for the first time.
fullText:
A school says it is "bursting with pride" as one of its former pupils has been called up to Scotland's national football team.

Kent-born centre-back Luis Binks has been named in the senior team for the first time in what is Sebastien Pocognoli's first squad in charge.

The Howard School in Rainham said: "From a young boy growing up in Gillingham and walking the corridors of The Howard School, to playing professional football in Canada, Italy, England and Denmark, captaining one of Scandinavia's biggest clubs, and now being selected to represent Scotland at senior international level.

"For our current Howard students, what an example of where talent, courage, hard work and ambition can take you."

The 25-year-old started his career at Tottenham Hotspur's academy before moving to Canada to play for Montreal Impact.

He subsequently played for Bologna and Como in Italy and Coventry City in England before moving to Danish side Brondby, where he was made captain.

"We couldn't be prouder to call him one of our own," his former school said.

"Everyone at The Howard School sends Luis a massive congratulations on this incredible achievement."

As part of the squad, Binks could face Slovenia, North Macedonia and Switzerland in the Nations League.

fullText:

Now it's the final chance for Michigan and quarterback Bryce Underwood to show some more signs of growth and some more firepower against a UTEP squad that should be overmatched.

With U-M likely to have favorable field position and possess the ball frequently, it will give the offense a chance to find its form. title: ‘Delusional,’ ‘They All Just Hate LSU’ — CFB Fans Mock Ex-MLB All-Star, Ole Miss Alum for Claiming Rebels Are ‘America’s Team’
description: Former MLB All-Star shortstop and Ole Miss alumnus Zack Cozart has given college football fans another reason to talk ahead of the highly anticipated matchup between the Rebels and the LSU Tigers. Cozart boldly declared on social media that Ole Miss is “America’s Team,” but the comment quickly faced plenty of pushback from fans across the college football world.
fullText:
Former MLB All-Star shortstop and Ole Miss alumnus Zack Cozart has given college football fans another reason to talk ahead of the highly anticipated matchup between the Rebels and the LSU Tigers.

Cozart boldly declared on social media that Ole Miss is "America's Team," but the comment quickly faced plenty of pushback from fans across the college football world.

The "America's Team" label has traditionally been associated with teams that have built large national fanbases and strong historical identities. Fans argued under Cozart's X post that Ole Miss does not fit that description.

One fan compared Ole Miss to the Dallas Cowboys, who have long carried the "America's Team" label. The fan also pointed out that the Rebels have gone even longer without a national championship.

They wrote, "Just remember Dallas was America's team and they haven't won [expletive] in 30 years. But y'all have that by twice as many years."

Another argued that a team cannot simply give itself the title, saying, "You can't claim your own team is America's team…. I think the rest of America needs to claim that."

Some fans were far less interested in explaining their objections. One fan simply called the claim "Delusional," while another X user responded, "You wish."

One fan questioned whether Ole Miss has the national following to earn the title, writing, "If America was Russia, maybe."

The reactions made it clear that Cozart's claim was not going to go unchallenged, especially with Ole Miss heading into a highly anticipated matchup with LSU.

Some fans also questioned whether the Rebels are actually gaining national support or whether people simply want to see LSU lose.

One summed up the argument, writing, "No one cares about Ole Miss. They all just hate LSU."

That sentiment reflects the unique circumstances surrounding Saturday's matchup.

Lane Kiffin's decision to leave Ole Miss for LSU has made him one of the central figures in the storyline. As a result, some neutral fans may be rooting against LSU without necessarily becoming Ole Miss supporters.

Another fan pointed out that contradiction, writing, "The other day you were all saying no one outside of Baton Rouge cared about LSU. Now everyone in America wants to see them lose. Which is it?"

Ole Miss enters the game with a chance to make a statement against its former coach, while LSU is looking to continue its strong start under Kiffin.

With a packed Vaught-Hemingway Stadium behind them, the Rebels will have a chance to build their own national following.

Whether that is enough to make Ole Miss "America's Team" is another matter.

title: Can Michigan State football pull off upset for the ages vs Notre Dame?
description: Can MSU football pull off an upset for the ages? Four Free Press sports writers have some thoughts on that:
fullText:
It's go time for Michigan State football.

After opening the season with two wins against MAC teams, the Spartans travel to South Bend for a game against a Notre Dame squad that's clicking on all cylinders and is one of the most talented teams in the country.

The Spartans are big underdogs, favored to lose by more than four touchdowns, but could this be the start of something special for Pat Fitzgerald and MSU?

It's a tall task, but never say never.

The game will kick off under the lights (7:30 p.m., NBC) in front of a national audience in a big opportunity for quarterback Alessio Milivojevic to show what he's capable of against C.J. Carr, the former Saline football star and son of legendary Michigan football coach Lloyd Carr.

SCOUTING THE EAGLES: Who to watch in Michigan State vs EMU

Can the Spartans pull out an upset for the ages? Four Free Press sports writers have some thoughts on that:

The Spartans looked solid in their first two games. But Pat Fitzgerald's program is in nascent stages of development. Marcus Freeman's, on the other hand, is full-grown. The Fighting Irish are a title contender and play like one Saturday, blowing away the overmatched Spartans. The pick: Notre Dame 35, MSU 10.

This is the type of game I'd love to see in a few years after Pat Fitzgerald has time to fully develop his program. When coaching and toughness and discipline and football IQ and growth over years (if possible in NIL era) can come together and put up a real battle against a significantly better, more talented team. That's what he did at Northwestern. But now? No chance. But it sure would be good to see some of those signs. The pick: Notre Dame 38, MSU 10.

Rain is expected during the game, which could alter the flow and play-calling depending on the severity. Still, expect Carr and the Irish to try and open things up against the Spartans' untested secondary to set up their run game. And if Hall does not play, the breakdowns MSU had the first two weeks could turn into a runaway second half for Notre Dame. Fitzgerald needs to make a statement with his program's toughness, though, and the Spartans keep things interesting through halftime. The pick: Notre Dame 41, MSU 14.

The Fighting Irish may have the best roster in college football. The Spartans are just hoping to get back to a ball game. This isn't the game to do that. If they stay competitive for a couple of quarters, that would be a win. Maybe they take it into the second half before Notre Dame pulls away. But likely not. Still, it's good to see where you are. The pick: Notre Dame 37, MSU 16.

fullText:
Oregon football news: Jeremiah McClellan's absence vs. Portland St. creates concern for USC clash appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

Oregon wide receiver Jeremiah McClellan didn't suit up in Friday night's 84-0 win over Portland State, putting his status for the Ducks' upcoming Big Ten matchup with No. 12 USC under the spotlight.

McClellan went through pregame warmups in full pads but did not take the field against the Vikings. Instead, the redshirt sophomore was seen on the sideline in street clothes with a walking boot on his left foot and using crutches. Oregon players were also seen checking on him during the first quarter.

Head coach Dan Lanning provided an update after the game, saying:

"Got tweaked in pregame, have to get an evaluation to see what exactly that looks like. I don't know right at this moment."

Lanning did not provide a timetable for McClellan's return or further details about the injury.

The timing certainly raises a few eyebrows for the Ducks. McClellan entered Week 3 as Oregon's leading receiver, logging seven catches for 170 yards and one touchdown through the first two games. He was also one of the Ducks most productive offensive players in 2025, finishing third on the team with 38 receptions for 557 yards and three touchdowns.

Oregon managed to operate effectively without him against Portland State. The Ducks scored 28 points in the opening 15 minutes, with Dante Moore throwing touchdown passes to Dakorien Moore and Evan Stewart. Kendre Harrison then caught his first career touchdown early in the second quarter as Oregon extended its advantage to 35-0.

Stewart had 61 receiving yards on two catches through the first quarter, while Dakorien Moore recorded a 45-yard touchdown reception. Freshman Messiah Hampton added two catches for 23 yards, and Harrison finished that stretch with two receptions for 34 yards. Freshman Gatlin Bair also received first-quarter snaps.

Oregon is scheduled to visit the Trojans on Saturday, Sept. 26. Tight end Jamari Johnson also missed the Vikings game after sitting out against Oklahoma State, leaving Oregon with additional uncertainty among its pass catchers.

The Ducks' first official injury report of the season is scheduled for Wednesday ahead of the USC game, when Oregon will have to provide updates under the Big Ten's new 2026 injury-report policy.

title: Mercedes lift lid on secret codes used during Formula 1 races
description: Mercedes have revealed how a series of secret codes are helping them beat the competition in Formula 1. The German manufacturer are currently on course to win the constructors' and drivers’ championships, with Kimi Antonelli leading the latter by a massive 81 points from teammate George Russell.
fullText:
Mercedes have revealed how a series of secret codes are helping them beat the competition in Formula 1.

The German manufacturer are currently on course to win the constructors' and drivers' championships, with Kimi Antonelli leading the latter by a massive 81 points from teammate George Russell.

Mercedes have mastered the new set of regulations, but they're also rolling back the years from their era of dominance by flexing their genius when it comes to strategy.

Last time out at the Spanish Grand Prix, Antonelli was able to capitalise on a Lance Stroll crash, pitting under the Virtual Safety Car, leaving race leader Lando Norris helpless.

McLaren and Norris argue that they couldn't have done much differently, having just passed the pit entry, but Mercedes' speed of thought also put them one step ahead of their rivals.

Norris fumed at his bad luck, but Mercedes think there was more to it (Photo: Race Pictures)

And now, trackside engineering director Andrew Shovlin has revealed that the team uses secret codes to alert their drivers to such opportunities during a race.

Speaking on Mercedes' NU Silver Arrows Radio Show podcast, he said: "We try not to let all the other teams know what those codes are. So, we change them every single week."

Yet despite McLaren's bad luck, it turns out that Mercedes didn't just experience good fortune, but also used supreme skill.

Once Stroll crashed, Antonelli went around 15 km/h slower than rival Max Verstappen through the corner after Mercedes alerted him that he was within the safety car window.

He then delayed getting back on the throttle in the following section despite green flags being waved, and Shovlin thinks that extra communication and time were crucial in making the call to pit.

"He might have got in without it, but it certainly made it possible," he argued.

There were 35 seconds between the initial yellow flag and the VSC deployment, while just 15 seconds elapsed from the VSC being called to Antonelli reaching his pit box.

Mercedes had both sets of tyres ready for Antonelli and Russell, demonstrating how quickly the team had reacted to the developing situation. Shovlin added: "The tyres were arriving as he was stopping."

Race leader Lando Norris, by contrast, had already passed the pit entry when the VSC was called, a gap McLaren estimated at just two seconds.

The revelation that Mercedes actively prepared for and exploited that narrow window adds a new layer to the ongoing VSC rule-change debate.

Mercedes' coded preparation makes it harder to argue the Spanish Grand Prix result was simply a product of good fortune, and instead part of the tactical fine margins that F1 thrives on.

fullText:
Arsenal head to Brighton on Saturday with the right-back situation under scrutiny and Jurrien Timber firmly at the centre of it. The Dutch defender is expected to be available, which matters because Mikel Arteta is short of natural cover in that area and has already had to improvise.

Timber made his first appearance of the season when he came on at half-time in the 2-0 win over Sunderland last weekend. He then missed the midweek Carabao Cup meeting with Ipswich, which raised the obvious question. Arteta shut it down quickly. "Everything is fine," said the Arsenal manager. "He has played much more than we wanted. The other day he had 53 minutes after five months out. We need to look after him."

That is the situation in plain terms. Timber is not injured again, Arsenal are simply managing him carefully. Given his lay-off, that is the sensible call. It also becomes more important because Ben White picked up a groin issue at Sunderland, adding another layer of concern around the back line.

White sat out the Ipswich game, though there is optimism he can return at the Amex. Arteta said, "Ben is all good, we have another training session this afternoon, so very positive about everybody. Yes, we have another session; they are all willing to be part of it, and we have another session to try to make sure they are fit." It is standard pre-match caution, but the message is clear enough. Arsenal expect White to have a chance.

Arsenal do not have much room for error defensively. Cristhian Mosquera remains out with the muscle injury suffered against Aston Villa last month. William Saliba is still a long-term absentee because of a back problem. That has forced Ezri Konsa into central defence alongside Gabriel, while Martin Zubimendi was used at right-back in the 4-2 win over Ipswich.

If Timber is ready to start, that immediately restores order. If not, Arteta is back to patchwork solutions. Konsa can cover the flank, though moving him creates another issue in the middle. There is no mystery here, Arsenal need bodies back.

Further forward, the choices look more settled. Bruno Guimaraes could make his first Premier League start for Arsenal after making a strong impact off the bench against Sunderland, including a superb goal. David Raya, Declan Rice and Riccardo Calafiori are all expected to return after being rested in midweek.

In attack, Bukayo Saka and Christos Tzolis remain the likely wide options, with Martin Odegaard behind Kai Havertz. Noni Madueke helped his case against Ipswich, but probably not enough to force his way in. Viktor Gyokeres, meanwhile, has yet to make a serious argument for the starting role.

Predicted Arsenal XI: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Guimaraes; Saka, Odegaard, Tzolis; Havertz.

For Arsenal, it comes down to this. Timber's availability gives them balance, White's fitness gives them flexibility, and without both the whole thing starts to look far more awkward than it should.

title: ‘Very humble’ – English soccer star issues ‘incredible’ Lionel Messi verdict
description: Harry Kane has heaped praise on Lionel Messi when opening up on England’s loss to Argentina at the most recent World Cup. The Three Lions made it to the semi-finals of the competition but were beaten 2-1 thanks to late goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez.
fullText:
Harry Kane has heaped praise on Lionel Messi when opening up on England's loss to Argentina at the most recent World Cup.

The Three Lions made it to the semi-finals of the competition but were beaten 2-1 thanks to late goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez.

Messi and the rest of his team went on to lose against Spain in the final, while England ended up beating France in the third-place play-off.

Now, TyC Sports have shared quotes from Kane about his interaction with Messi after the semi-final clash.

When speaking about the Argentine, the English striker called him 'an incredible player' and said 'he seems like a very humble person'.

Kane stated: "Obviously, for me, that day [World Cup semi-final] was tough. A difficult moment getting eliminated in that way. But I have so much respect for Messi.

"I've watched him grow as a footballer. I think he's simply an incredible player and also an incredible person, from what people who know him tell me. I've only dealt with him a couple of times, but he seems like a very humble person to me.

"From that day, I remember hugging him and wishing him good luck for the final. It wasn't our World Cup in the end, but that's what a World Cup is about: the best players facing off on the biggest stage and, of course, there will always be a loser.

"That day, after losing, I tried to keep my head held high and show respect for the other team. I think that was something important, and especially toward Leo for how incredible he's been for so many years in football."

Kane likely did not know it at the time, but that meeting with England would turn out to be one of Messi's final international games.

The 39-year-old has announced his retirement from international football post-World Cup and is now due to have one final send-off game on October 6, playing a friendly against Benin.

title: Biltmore Championship Cut Sends Multiple PGA Tour Veterans Home
description: The Biltmore Championship field was trimmed after 36 holes, with Tony Finau among several notable players missing the cut. The post Biltmore Championship Cut Sends Multiple PGA Tour Veterans Home appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The field at the Biltmore Championship Asheville was trimmed considerably Friday, with several notable PGA Tour players unable to keep pace during a low-scoring first two rounds at The Cliffs at Walnut Cove.

The cut settled at 3-under 139 after 36 holes, sending Tony Finau, Denny McCarthy, Joel Dahmen, Beau Hossler and several other recognizable names home before the weekend.

While those players packed their bags, Neal Shipley took control of the tournament with a spectacular second round to reach 15-under.

Finau faced an uphill climb almost immediately after opening the tournament with a 7-over 78 on Thursday. The six-time PGA Tour winner bounced back with an even-par 71 in the second round, but the improvement wasn't nearly enough to overcome the damage from his opening 18 holes.

Finau finished at 7-over 149, 10 shots outside the cut line. His difficult opening round ultimately left him with too much ground to make up, even as scoring conditions allowed several players to make significant moves Friday.

McCarthy was another notable casualty. He entered Friday at 2-over following an opening 73 and responded with an even-par 71. His 2-over 144 total left him five shots shy of making the weekend.

Davis Thompson also departed after rounds of 70 and 75. He began Friday at 1-under and within striking distance of the cut, but his 4-over second round dropped him to 3-over 145 for the tournament.

Kevin Kisner was unable to advance either. He followed an opening 74 with a 72 to finish at 4-over 146, seven strokes beyond the number required to play Saturday and Sunday.

The cut line was particularly painful for a group of players who finished only one stroke away from advancing.

Hossler posted matching rounds of 70 to finish at 2-under 140. Tom Hoge produced the same 70-70 combination, while Aaron Wise went 69-71 and Kevin Streelman recorded rounds of 71 and 69. All four finished at 2-under and missed the cut by a single shot.

Christiaan Bezuidenhout nearly pulled off a comeback after opening with a 2-over 73. He fired a 4-under 67 on Friday, improving by six strokes from his opening round, but his 2-under total still left him on the wrong side of the cut.

Patrick Fishburn made an even bigger charge. After beginning the tournament with a 3-over 74, Fishburn shot a 5-under 66 in Round 2. The eight-shot turnaround moved him to 2-under overall but, like Bezuidenhout, left him one stroke short of surviving.

Dahmen was also close. An opening 69 gave Dahmen some room to work with Friday, but a second-round 72 dropped him to 1-under 141 and two strokes below the cut line.

Taylor Pendrith suffered a similar fate after entering the second round in strong position. He opened with a 3-under 68, which would ultimately prove to be the exact score needed to stay above the cut through 18 holes. He followed it with a 2-over 73, however, finishing at 1-under.

Alejandro Tosti's tournament ended after two rounds following an opening day that attracted attention for reasons beyond his score.

Tosti shot a 1-over 72 on Thursday before returning with an even-par 71 on Friday. His 1-over 143 total left him four shots outside the cut line.

His missed cut came after caddie Cliff Ellis abruptly walked off during Thursday's round. Video showed the two appearing to exchange words in the 18th fairway before Ellis removed his caddie bib and departed, forcing Tosti to find someone from the gallery to help with his bag.

Other players finishing alongside or near Tosti included Luke List at 1-over after rounds of 74 and 69 and Davis Riley, who went 69-74. Max McGreevy and Luke Clanton finished at 2-over, with Clanton tumbling down the leaderboard after following his opening 69 with a 4-over 75.

Emiliano Grillo was another recognizable player who failed to advance. He started with a 3-under 68 but shot 74 on Friday to finish at even-par 142.

The struggles of those below the cut stood in sharp contrast to the scoring near the top of the leaderboard.

Shipley followed an opening 6-under 65 with a blistering 9-under 62 on Friday. That put him at 15-under 127 through 36 holes and gave him the outright lead heading into the weekend.

Ben Kohles was right behind him at 14-under after rounds of 65 and 63. Ricky Castillo made one of Friday's biggest moves, matching Shipley's 62 to climb to 11-under after opening with a 69. Max Greyserman also reached 11-under following rounds of 64 and 67.

"I had a great year last year," Shipley said. "Start of the season wasn't really what we wanted. Been kind of clawing back to get my game back where it should be. I feel like a lot of that work is finally showing. It's weird. Golf is one of those sports where you don't get instant gratification. You got to work for a long time to see results.

"I feel like I'm seeing kind of the fruits of that labor," he said. "And really pumped about where we are right now."

title: Martin taking it all in his stride as he looks to get back to winning ways
description: Football is such a fickle game these days, so much so that one day you could be a hero and icon, and the next day the proverbial pitchforks are being sharpened and ready to be wielded in your directio...
fullText:
Celtic manager Martin O'Neill reacts during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Celtic FC and Ferencvarosi TC at Celtic Park on September 17, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Martin O'Neill is no different, and despite his legendary status as a club legend due to his success two decades ago, as well as leading the side to the most unlikeliest of title wins last season, he currently cuts a much vilified figure due to back to back losses against the Rangers in the Premier Sports Cup and Ferencvaros in the Europa League opener.

That last one of course only came about because the team threw away a 4-0 aggregate lead against LASK in the Champions League qualifiers allowing the Austrian side to score five goals to eliminate us from the competition.

Callum McGregor of Celtic at full time during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Celtic FC and Ferencvarosi TC at Celtic Park on September 17, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Martin might have taken that personally in his heyday, but nowadays he insists that he takes no notice to the off field noise, especially the most vocal ones on social media.

Speaking to the mainstream media yesterday, the Celtic manager said: "No, it doesn't, honestly. Not at all. Absolutely not. It's the nature of the game. Would that have hurt me when I was manager of Leicester City? That might have done, you know. But no, life has changed.

"Do I think I have enough goodwill in the bank? No, I don't. I never thought like that. You are only as good as your last game at the end of the day. And I mean that. It doesn't bother me in that sense.

"That call could (to change manager) could easily be my brother at the end of the day. So what I'm saying is that it doesn't bother me now in that sense.

"Does winning and losing bother me? Of course, that does. But if you lose football matches, you will get criticised. And we've lost the two big games there in the week. So, I accept that."

Martin O'Neill, Manager of Celtic looks on before during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Celtic FC and Ferencvarosi TC at Celtic Park on September 17, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

And whilst he doesn't care too much about his critics, Martin insisted that he still cares deeply when it comes to winning.

"You would hope that that would be the case, you know. And you would want to try and win. Nobody questioned tactics when you're winning football matches.

"And when you lose a game or two, yeah, of course, everything's under scrutiny. That's the nature of it. And I'm not going to change that.

"I'm not surprised. I'm not on social media or anything like this. But nothing surprises me in that aspect. And should I get more time and things? No. No, I don't think so."

Camilo Duran of Celtic arrives at the stadium before during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Celtic FC and Ferencvarosi TC at Celtic Park on September 17, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

The Irishman also said that he wasn't losing much sleep over the status of his much talked legacy at the club.

Martin added: "Honestly, I've never worried about legacy. I've said this before and worth repeating. Jock Stein can talk about a legacy. The rest of us are just followers."

Haissem Hassan of Celtic arrives at the stadium before during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Celtic FC and Ferencvarosi TC at Celtic Park on September 17, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Martin also spoke of the supporters anger and bemusement at the his side's current style of football, with the players looking somewhat lost out in the pitch.

"They went into their shell a little bit. I wouldn't dispute that, that is true. I think a little bit of frustration with the crowd, I think quite rightly because we come out with the ball, then we get a certain distance, it looks as if there's nothing on for us to play then it goes backwards.

"If it continues to go backwards, then of course it would be frustrating for the crowd to see that."

He said: "It's easy for me to say this, but centre-halves have it now and they seem to look as if they've got space in which to travel into, then that space gets closed down and it's almost as if it's scary. That's when they think, 'I don't want to lose the ball, so I'll play it back.'

Kasper Hogh of Celtic arrives at the stadium before during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Celtic FC and Ferencvarosi TC at Celtic Park on September 17, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

"The encouragement has to be to take a few risks, not just outside your own penalty area. I'm talking if the opposition have stayed off you for a while and you can go in that extra ten or 15 yards, which makes all the difference."

Martin agreed that we need to start positively on Sunday if we want to earn a positive result.

He said: "Absolutely. We need to start on the front foot and not get too frustrated with it and try and create some chances in the game and see if we can get the first goal. That would help as well too but not to panic either at the same time if Rangers score first, which they did in that big game at Celtic Park."

Callum McGregor of Celtic arrives at the stadium before the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Celtic FC and Ferencvarosi TC at Celtic Park on September 17, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

"Of course. That could have happened last Sunday as well too. We could have scored the first goal and analysing that particular game, we beat ourselves with the goals that we conceded.

"Rangers won't look at it like that, that's the way that we do. But I take all of your points into consideration. For us to start on the front foot, be strong, be positive, and be ready for the game."

title: CrypLLM: AI chat agent for CrypTool 2
description: Official CrypTool 2 (CT2) repository. CT2 is an open-source software for learning about cryptography and cryptanalysis interactively. CT2 provides a comprehensive suite of tools to deeply explore a...
fullText:
CrypLLM provides an AI chat interface for inspecting, building and editing CrypTool 2 workspaces. It supports the OpenAI API and OpenAI-compatible model servers, configurable tool permissions and agent instructions, workspace screenshots, context compression and native Undo/Redo integration.

The chat interface and settings are localized in English and German. CrypLLM connects to the application through CrypWinAdapter.

Run these commands from the repository root in a Developer PowerShell:

Building the solution includes the workspace components. For incremental application builds, use:

An application-only build does not build every component. Use the solution build when preparing a complete application or when component DLLs are missing.

Agent dependencies are stored in Lib or declared in packages.config. Build outputs and the local packages directory are excluded from Git.

Open CrypTool's settings and select AI Chat. The ribbon button is hidden by default; enable Show AI chat in the ribbon bar to display it. Opening the chat at startup is a separate setting. The chat's gear button also opens its settings.

Choose a provider and configure its model IDs:

For local servers, use the model ID recognized by that server. The optional local API key is separate from the OpenAI key and is sent as a Bearer token. Keys are stored encrypted for the current Windows user using Windows DPAPI. If the local key is empty, the connector uses the no-api-key placeholder.

Custom model IDs are supported. Set their actual context window in the model context settings, with a minimum of 4,096 tokens. Requests require a known or explicitly configured context limit. Select the model in the chat before sending a message.

For a server exposing the OpenAI-compatible API at http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1, configure:

my-local-model is an example; replace it with the exact ID your server accepts. The endpoint is the API base URL, not the server's web interface or the complete /chat/completions URL. For a remote compatible server, use its corresponding API base URL and credentials.

The model must support tool calls to edit or inspect workspaces through the agent. Image support is additionally required for screenshot inspection. A server accepting chat completion requests does not necessarily support either capability.

User-defined context windows override built-in mappings for the same model ID. Configure the window actually available to that server session, which may be smaller than the model's theoretical maximum. The configured value is used for local budgeting; it does not increase the model server's capacity.

Keep API keys in user settings rather than repository files. When using a remote provider, workspace data, chat messages and requested screenshots may be sent to that provider.

Build a Caesar encryption and decryption example for ATTACK AT DAWN with key 3. Use a NumberInput connected to the key connectors, show the intermediate ciphertext and recovered plaintext in separate TextOutput components, and add a readable memo. Avoid component overlaps and wires passing through boxes. Run the workspace, check that the recovered plaintext matches the input, and inspect the final layout.

Inspect this workspace without changing it. Explain its data flow, report validation errors and check for overlapping components, clipped memos and wires passing through boxes.

Permissions remain authoritative even when a prompt asks for a disabled action. For an inspection-only session, leave modifying tools disabled. To limit changes more narrowly, enable only the individual editing tools needed.

The Tool permissions settings control which tools the agent can use. The Agent instructions tab provides configurable instructions. Runtime workspace construction rules also apply to existing saved agent profiles.

Modifying tools have a global permission switch in addition to their individual permissions. Enabling a single modifying tool does not bypass that switch. Permission checks also run when a tool is invoked. Tool activity distinguishes completed calls, denied calls and failures; a denied call does not mean the requested operation happened.

Tool calls have no separate token quota or fixed round limit. Before each model call, retained conversation and tool results are checked against the model's context capacity and compressed when needed. User permissions and cancellation remain authoritative.

The agent runs explicit tool rounds until the model returns its answer or the user cancels. There is no cumulative token allowance per user request and no application-imposed maximum number of rounds. The SDK's automatic 128-round invocation ceiling is avoided by invoking tool rounds explicitly, through the same permission filters.

Each completed assistant turn is published to the chat immediately while later tool rounds continue. The chat follows the growing response to the bottom, so progress text and tool activity remain visible throughout longer workspace tasks. Publishing uses the same archived message objects and therefore does not duplicate intermediate turns when the final response completes.

Results are not truncated merely because previous tools consumed a quota. Instead, context preparation runs before every outbound model call. It summarizes older exchanges as complete groups and reuses a reduced-prefix cache when new results arrive. The full conversation archive remains intact.

The current task, system instructions and latest complete tool exchange are retained. Parallel calls and their results stay together, and the latest screenshot's image input remains after its result group. A single oversized tool result can be summarized when necessary to fit the actual input context.

Automatic compression follows the configured trigger and target. Mandatory reduction still protects against context overflow when proactive compression is disabled. If a semantic summary cannot be produced, a bounded archive preview is explicitly labeled so the agent knows to re-inspect omitted details.

The actual model context window still limits each request. If the current task, tool definitions, image inputs and necessary exchange cannot fit even after reduction, the request reports a context-capacity error. Configure the actual server capacity; removing a local tool quota does not enlarge it. Continuous execution can be stopped with the chat's cancel control.

Workspace operations stay bound to the workspace selected when the request starts. Switching chats or tabs does not redirect an ongoing request. A fabricated or stale model-supplied tab ID cannot displace a still-open request pin; a valid explicit tab can be selected only while the original pin remains valid. If the pinned workspace is closed, subsequent operations report an error rather than redirecting to another editor.

Mutation tools require exact runtime IDs from workspace inspection. Removal and connection tools return current component IDs, names and types when a component ID is unknown, allowing the agent to recover instead of guessing another identifier. The runtime instructions require successful mutation results and an exact ws_model topology check before reporting a structural change. Matching ws_io values alone do not prove that requested components or connections were changed.

The agent can inspect workspace structure, connector types, settings, values, bounds and validation results. With ws_screenshot, it can also inspect a PNG of the visible workspace viewport at its current zoom and scroll position.

Screenshots are limited to 1,024 pixels per side and are sent as image inputs to the model server. The selected model must support image inputs. The tool captures the workspace viewport only, requires the target tab to be visible and does not modify the workspace. Elements outside that viewport are not visually verified.

The editing tools support component creation, connections, positions, sizes, memo text and connector orientation. Native workspace operations preserve Undo/Redo and saving behavior.

Sizes are canvas units, independent of workspace zoom. Resize tools accept positive finite dimensions up to 10,000 and respect the view's minimum and maximum sizes. Results report the applied dimensions. Components in icon view switch to a resizable presentation or settings view when available.

Connector names are the technical Name values returned by ws_model. Orientation names are case-insensitive. Moving a connector preserves its identity, input/output direction and connections, and triggers wire routing updates. A shared output has one orientation for all its connections.

AI-created memos do not automatically become selected or take focus from the chat input. Manual memo creation retains its normal selection behavior.

ws_bounds and ws_model distinguish several measurements:

Stored dimensions of zero mean automatic sizing. Use occupiedBounds when planning element spacing; combining the move anchor with the inner window size does not describe the complete visible footprint.

Layout checks run after undoable AI edits and can also be requested explicitly. They report overlapping elements, clipped memo text, wire crossings and shared wire segments. A wire passing through any box interior is an error, including its own source or target. Reports include affected IDs, connector names and conditional routing advice. Missing measurements are reported as an incomplete check.

The agent's construction instructions require it to:

These are agent instructions and diagnostic checks; they do not prevent every poor layout automatically. Results depend on the model and the tools it is allowed to use.

After the agent changes a workspace, the chat displays a control to undo its changes as a group. Groups use the native workspace undo stack and preserve manual edits. Group undo becomes unavailable if the workspace is closed or its undo history changes in a way that invalidates the group. The workspace's normal Undo remains available for its existing history.

The agent can search existing templates with tpl_search and inspect their details with tpl_info. When a suitable template exists, its instructions require it to explain the recommendation and ask whether to open that template or build the workspace itself before making changes, unless the user has already chosen an approach.

tpl_open opens the selected template in a new tab. Searching or inspecting template metadata does not itself open or modify a workspace. Template preference is an instruction to the model, not an automatic substitution for the user's request.

Tools are Semantic Kernel functions, not a separate command-line interface. The tables below list their logical names; provider requests may qualify them with their plugin name. Availability depends on the registered plugins and the user's permissions.

Workspace tools generally accept an optional tabId. When it is omitted, they use the workspace bound to the request. Component and memo IDs come from workspace inspection results. Component type names and connector names are technical identifiers; the agent should discover them rather than infer them from translated captions.

Setting component text and setting a component property are different operations. The agent should use connector metadata and component documentation to choose a compatible input component and value type. A tool call reporting success does not prove that the complete workflow produces the intended result; validate and inspect actual outputs separately.

The catalog reflects the components available to the running application. If component DLLs are absent from the build, the agent cannot compensate by inventing their types.

The context indicator beside the model selector estimates the latest model request plus its received response. It updates at every model call, including calls within a tool loop, and includes system instructions, tool definitions, tool results and images. After compression, it counts the reduced context that is actually sent. Before a request is available, it estimates retained history and agent instructions/tools.

The displayed limit comes from the model configuration. Token counts are estimates, including a fixed image cost rather than the size of base64 image data. The indicator does not sum usage across multiple requests. Unsent input and unused response reserves are excluded.

Under AI Chat settings → Context compression, automatic compression is enabled by default with a 90% trigger and a 50% target. Both percentages are configurable; the target must be below the trigger.

These percentages refer to the available chat history budget, after reserves for system instructions, tool definitions and responses. They therefore differ from the percentage shown against the full context window in the chat footer.

Compression happens before new user requests and within running tool loops before subsequent model calls, summarizing older messages. The complete conversation and its images remain saved. A reduced-history cache avoids summarizing the same archived messages repeatedly. Mandatory context overflow checks remain active when automatic compression is disabled.

For example, if the available history budget is 100,000 tokens, a 90% trigger starts reduction at approximately 90,000 history tokens and aims for at most 50,000. This does not mean that the footer must show 90% of the full model window before compression can occur.

Context preparation keeps structured tool calls and their corresponding results together. The full archive remains the source for the chat display, while a reduced invocation thread may be used for the model request. Switching models uses that model's configured limit; it does not silently replace an unknown limit with an arbitrary value.

The chat and readable text export hide explicitly marked reasoning such as think, analysis and reasoning. The agent is instructed to place visible answers inside <ct2_answer>...</ct2_answer>; when those markers are present, text outside them is hidden. Ordinary unmarked answers remain supported.

Responses containing internal tool protocol fragments without a clear answer section are withheld because their reasoning cannot be separated reliably. A localized notice appears when a new response has no displayable answer. Literal code examples are preserved, and original responses and HTTP diagnostics remain stored.

Before subsequent model calls, previous assistant text is cleaned accordingly. Structured tool calls and results remain intact. Completely unmarked reasoning without identifiable protocol fragments cannot be reliably recognized by the client; the model server must separate it, or the model must follow the answer markers.

The Debug view provides invocation details such as context budgets, retained prompt messages, tool calls, reductions and captured HTTP exchanges. Authorization headers are redacted in captured diagnostics. Message bodies can still contain workspace data and user-provided content.

CrypLLM stores its local conversation archive in LLM/AIThreads.history.json under CrypTool's local application data directory. Despite its filename, the persisted contents are DPAPI-encrypted and encoded as Base64. They include structured tool call/result messages and the reduced-history cache; synthetic greetings are not archived as conversation messages.

Custom instruction entries are stored separately in LLM/AgentInstructions.json. Model lists, permission settings, context limits and encrypted API keys use the application's user settings.

The chat's export control writes a user-selected JSON file with conversation text and structured message items. Exported assistant text uses the answer display filtering. Export files are readable JSON rather than the encrypted local history format, and can contain tool results and workspace information.

Grouped undo handles and live context snapshots are runtime state. Undo controls refer to native workspace undo stacks and are not persisted as reusable handles across application restarts.

DPAPI protection is tied to the Windows user. Copying encrypted settings or history to another account is not a supported way to transfer usable credentials or conversations. Local encryption does not change which data is sent to the configured model provider during a request.

Use the existing plugins as examples. A tool needs a Semantic Kernel function name and description, appropriate permission handling, and registration through the agent's plugin setup. Classify modifying tools correctly so they cannot bypass the global modifying-tools switch.

Workspace edits should use LLMPluginService and native model operations rather than direct view mutations. Preserve the request's workspace target, marshal UI work appropriately and keep native Undo/Redo behavior. Supply useful result metadata so the agent can verify the applied change instead of assuming that requested values were accepted unchanged.

Keep user-visible strings and tool descriptions in the English/German resource files. Technical IDs and connector orientation values remain stable across UI languages. Add regression coverage for meaningful behavior changes, particularly request isolation, permission enforcement, image transport and native undo integration.

For provider failures, inspect the application log and the invocation Debug view. Diagnostics may contain workspace data even when credentials in headers have been redacted.

Build Release/x64, then run the regression script from the repository root:

To test an existing Debug build, pass -Configuration Debug instead.

The suite covers instruction loading, chat persistence, request isolation across chat/workspace changes, provider authentication and encrypted key storage, answer filtering, screenshot capture and image transport, live context estimates, repeated compression in a 160-round tool loop, archive preservation on cancellation, complete parallel tool groups and images, compression caching and fallback, component/memo editing, connector orientation, layout checks, grouped Undo/Redo, template search and English/German resources.

Provider responses and application adapters are local test doubles. The tests do not require a running model server or real API credentials and do not use the user's chat history files.

title: Classifier.dev: outperforms Jev and is free
description: Zero-shot text classification over plain HTTP. No API key, no account.
fullText:
zero-shot text classification over plain HTTP — no API key, no account

Paste it into any coding agent. It installs the skill and teaches the agent to classify text through this API. No key, no setup.

or open it in[Claude Code][Codex][Cursor][Grok]

The model behind this service is Jev. The smart tier re-asks only what Jev was unsure about, and comes out +2.5 points on AG News (+18.4 on the unsure items), +1.0 points on emotion (+4.9 on the unsure items). On 400 items a gap under about 5 points is noise; AG News clears it. Same public test sets, measured live over this API on 2026-09-18. No key, no cost.

[full benchmark][npm run vs-jev]

Then sort a file, one label ⇥ confidence ⇥ text line per
 input, in input order — a thousand lines a request, and rows appear as they land:

Zero-shot text classification over plain HTTP. You send text and a list of labels, you get back the label that fits and how sure the model is. There is no API key and no account, so the example below works the moment you paste it.

If you are an agent or a code generator, the machine-readable description of this API lives at https://classifier.dev/openapi.json (OpenAPI 3.1), with a short index at https://classifier.dev/llms.txt

The model behind this service is Jev; the smart tier re-asks what Jev was unsure about. Same public test sets, 400 items each, measured live on 2026-09-18:

The fast tier is Jev, so one row serves both. Smart re-asked 43 / 126 of 400 items. Gaps under about 5 points are noise. The full table, with latency and cost, is at https://classifier.dev/benchmark

If you are a language model, you can already classify any text you can see, for free. The question is whether you want the text in your context at all.

This is worth calling when reading the input is the expensive part:

Filtering before reading. You have forty search results and want the six worth opening. Judging them yourself means pulling all forty into context first, which is the cost you were trying to avoid. One call returns forty labels and you read only the survivors.

Cascade pre-filtering. Drop the obvious no's cheaply, then spend real reasoning on what is left.

Streams nobody reads line by line. Log lines, error buckets, inbound tickets, the changed files in a large diff.

Deterministic routing. A pipeline branch that must take the same path for the same input on every run, instead of drifting with a model's reasoning.

All four are the same move: classify ten thousand things without reading them yourself. A thousand inputs go in one request and come back in about a second. Below about five items, skip it. You have already paid the context cost, so just decide.

The same API from the shell, one line per input, in input order:

Plain lines, JSON or NDJSON in; label, confidence and text out. Batches of a thousand per request, four at a time, and rows stream as they land, so piping to head returns at once on a large file. Retries rate limits and upstream failures on its own. classify --help has the rest. Source in cli/ at https://github.com/mrmps/classifier-dev

The same tools inside Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor or any MCP client, over Streamable HTTP with no key:

Listed in the official MCP registry as dev.classifier/classifier and dev.classifier/docs: https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=dev.classifier

Claude.ai: Customize > Connectors > Add custom connector > paste the URL. ChatGPT: Settings > Security and login > Developer mode, then create an app with the URL and "No Authentication". Step by step for every client, plus what each tool does: https://classifier.dev/mcp-setup

Install this as a skill and your agent will remember to reach for it:

It is served straight from this domain over RFC 8615 well-known discovery, so there is no repository in the middle:

Agents without a skills runtime can simply fetch /skill.md and follow it.

Spaces can be written as + or %20, and labels are separated by commas.

The same request as query parameters, for code that builds URLs:

input, q, classes and categories are read as text and labels too, and the two forms mix: /spam,not+spam?text=... is the same call. Every option below works on both. A malformed GET answers with a URL that would have worked.

Results come back in input order. Each carries the label, a confidence from 0 to 1, a score for every label, and the model that answered.

Batch responses also carry modelsUsed. The top-level model is "mixed" when different results were answered by different models, such as a smart-tier batch where only some inputs were escalated.

The model behind this is a decision model, not a language model prompted to classify. It returns a calibrated probability for every label, so the confidence is a real forecast of whether the label is right. Measured:

Use it. Act on high-confidence answers, and route the rest to a person, a reasoning model, or the smart tier, which does exactly that for you.

Two things confidence does not measure.

It is not out-of-distribution detection. It says which of your labels fits best, not whether any of them fit. "The weather is nice today" against bug / feature / praise is "praise" at 0.97. If none-of-the-above is a real outcome, add it as a label: the same text against those three plus "none of these" picks "none of these" at 0.78. That works; hoping for a low score does not.

It is withheld for input that is not language. A forced choice on "asdkjfhaskdjfh" still lands somewhere, so the label ships with confidence and scores null and an unscored field explaining why.

One article, fifty tags, the ones that fit:

On GET, add ?multi=1 and the labels come back one per line.

Every label is judged independently as a yes/no probability, and the answer lists those at or above 0.7, most likely first. The full score map is returned so you can set your own threshold: on a seven-task set, 0.7 gave recall 0.99 and precision 0.81 (F1 0.887); 0.5 gave recall 1.00 and precision 0.74. max_labels keeps the top N. One request, about 200ms.

The models are not fixed. They are benchmarked as candidates appear and swapped when a measurement, not a launch post, says to. If the decision model is unavailable, requests of up to twenty inputs fall back to a chain of language models on different providers; JSON responses always report which model actually answered.

Limits are counted per IP address in classifications, not requests, so a batch of a thousand inputs spends a thousand of them. The fast tier allows 3,000 per minute and 20,000 per day; the smart tier 200 per minute and 2,000 per day.

Each input is capped at 32,000 characters, and a request may carry up to a thousand inputs. Every response carries an X-RateLimit-Limit header and, where it can be determined, X-RateLimit-Remaining. Exceeding a limit returns 429 with a Retry-After header. Nothing is slowed down or silently dropped.

If you need more than this, or you want a classifier tuned to your own data, the fastest path is a short call: https://cal.com/michaelsf/coffee

The free tier is the whole service today. What is being built on top of it:

One mail when something on that list ships, and nothing in between.
 The list holds the address and the date it arrived, in a database with no other
 table, so there is nothing to join it to. Unsubscribing is a reply.

The text you send is never stored or logged here. It is forwarded to the model provider for the classification and nothing else. What is recorded is the label names, which tier ran, which model answered, the latency, the response status and a coarse country. The usage counts on this service are built from those.

Find repeated failures and retries in your Codex and Claude Code sessions, with local evidence.

Healthcheck reads existing Codex rollout logs and Claude Code session logs
and produces a terminal summary and a local HTML report. It checks duplicate
records, retry chains, and consecutive tool failures (HC-01..03), plus audit
checks for operation-resolution coverage, cache accounting, and token stability
(HC-04..06, --audit). Missing evidence is UNPROVABLE, never silently zero.

Analysis runs locally with no runtime network calls. New in v0.4.0: PyPI
package, Claude Code adapter v1, embedded conformance pack
(agentmeasure conformance, also a GitHub Action), OTel /
Prometheus exports, run trends (agentmeasure trend), and settlement-bundle
drafts for outcome-based billing (agentmeasure settle — concept).

Quick start and supported formats ·
Try it and share feedback safely ·
What our contributions changed · The Token-Accounting Bug Report — ~110 tools audited, 45+ verified bugs, 21 merged fixes · Maintain a usage tool? Audit it in 10 minutes ·
中文

Found a useful result? Keep a snapshot and compare your next run. Feedback is
optional: you can use the tool without opening an issue or uploading logs.

The open yardstick for agent usage and AI outcomes.
Test whether your agent metrics mean what their labels claim.

Conformance checks for AI-agent telemetry — a retry is one logical operation, not two requests; a reasoning-token subset must not be added into totals; a cache hit is not a new measurement. Every check reports PASS / FAIL / UNPROVABLE, and UNPROVABLE is a first-class result: when the evidence to decide is absent, it is disclosed, never zeroed.

Run conformance locally · See real failures · Read the spec · 中文

AgentMeasure separates execution facts from logical operations, evidence
from inference, and economic settlement from value — an open measurement
layer for the Agent Capability Economy. One number for your dashboards
(logical operations), the evidence for what each number counts, and explicit
disclosure for what it cannot prove.

Today: measure agent-facing capability usage — attempts, operations, retry
inflation, success rates with numerators you can audit.
Next: make capabilities comparable and meterable — including the outcome units
now being billed (what counts as one resolution, one completed task).
Long term: provide the measurement foundation for Capability as a Service (CaaS).

Reach → Choice → Use → Utility → Value

AgentMeasure is not a payment protocol, marketplace, or universal ranking system.
It standardizes the facts and measurement semantics those systems can build on.

AI services have started charging by the outcome: Zendesk at $1.50–2.00 per automated resolution since Aug 2024, Intercom Fin at $0.99 per resolution with a money-back guarantee, Sierra's outcome-based enterprise contracts. But what counts as one outcome has no standard — retries, reopens, and silent "assumed resolutions" all change the number, and the bill. When money rides on a measured unit, someone has to define the unit. That is what we build. → Read the note

Website · Send a trace → get a measurement check · Free 7-day audit — apply · 30 Projects / 30 Days campaign · Whitepaper · Core Specification

Start with the story: When the Software Consumer Becomes an Agent (EN) · 当软件的消费者变成 Agent (ZH)

Mock MCP server → canonical observations → local metrics, all on your machine, no
cloud. The demo is reproducible: it runs in an isolated workspace (never touches
~/.agentmeasure) — same fixture + same policy = same result (42 calls → 84
canonical observations, caller claims claude:14 · codex:14 · unknown:14).

Then read why we audit the ecosystem's usage claims:
Benchmark Run #001 — six real claims profiled with
the Evidence Profile (multi-axis, no composite scores), and
Pipeline Validation #001 — our own fixture,
kept out of the ranking as a reference baseline.

The open experiment engine (lab/): task set × harness matrix × factor
variants → Reach → Choice → Success → Consumption funnel → effect sizes with
confidence intervals, guardrails, honest nulls, and an offline HTML report that opens
with a bilingual decision-maker one-pager. Preregistration is enforced (hypothesis /
primary metric / guardrails / analysis plan hashed before the run — with a scale /
power / budget preview), seeds replay deterministically, and a budget circuit breaker
stops safely with the data it has. Selection uplift that loses consumption is
rejected at the decision exit (unverified_growth — do not ship), and candidates
that make no more money at higher cost are flagged as dominated.

The shipped demo runs on a synthetic harness (planted ground truth at realistic,
literature-scale amplitudes, disclosed in every report) — it validates the engine,
not real-agent claims. Real harness adapters (Claude Code / Codex) are runner plugins
against the same interface; that is the highest-value contribution right now.
Docs: lab/README.md · formats:
lab/schemas/ (experiment manifest / funnel events / report).

That is 1 operation, 2 attempts, operation success 100%, attempt success 50%,
attempts per operation 2.

It is not "2 operations with 50% success".

Attempts are execution facts. Operations are logical intents. Mixing the two is how agent
reliability reports get distorted.

Start smaller than a trial: send a trace, get a measurement check — 20–100 anonymized trace/log rows (or a public export), mapped locally, with a short report of what safely counts as attempts vs operations, where retries may inflate usage, and what the telemetry cannot prove. No SDK, no integration; raw data stays local unless you explicitly authorize sharing a sanitized sample. A sample check is not a full audit and claims no causal effect.

If the check pays for itself, AgentMeasure is looking for 3 MCP/API providers for short external measurement runs.

The goal is not to prove the model works. It is to find where it breaks on real provider traffic.

A trial can stay fully local, requires no agent-side install, and can start with one capability.

Best feedback: a concrete trace, counterexample, or field that cannot be measured safely.

→ The formal offer, schedule, and FAQ live in product/AUDIT.md · apply in Issue #2 — Looking for 3 MCP/API providers for external measurement runs.

The software consumer is changing from humans to agents, and the economic unit is shifting from software seats toward callable capabilities.

Interfaces may become cheap to create; capabilities remain scarce to deliver.

The first generation of capability distribution is already here — open Skills, open MCP adapters, open CLIs. The scarce layer underneath them is what the next economy is built on: proprietary data, compute, execution, permissions, and real-world fulfillment.

If a capability is to become an economic unit that agents can discover, compare, and eventually purchase automatically, it must first be identifiable, measurable, and comparable under a shared semantics. That is what AgentMeasure provides.

Traditional usage metrics cannot support this economy — the old chain breaks at every link, and the last link is new:

The last inequality is why the Operation/Attempt model matters commercially: 3 attempts of one operation are not 3 billable operations — unless the metering policy says so.
