fullText:
Dating back to his days as an NFL quarterback, Ryan Fitzpatrick has been a favorite of both the media and fans.

The journeyman was a great quote for reporters and hosts, and lived up to the notion that backup quarterbacks are always the fan favorite on a team. Several of Fitzpatrick's late-season runs — in Houston, New York, Buffalo and Miami — will are still remembered fondly by the fans of those franchises.

Since joining the Prime Video crew on Thursday Night Football, Fitzpatrick has remained a daring darling of the football community. The big-bearded QB was in Buffalo for the opening of Highmark Stadium, and celebrated with a traditional leap through a folding table.

It went over great in the building, but somewhere in New York City, FS1's Nick Wright watched with bemusement. Friday on First Things First as the show aired a highlight of Fitzpatrick's table-crash, Wright questioned the hype.

"We don't need to promote this guy. It's enough. He gets plenty of promotion," Wright said.

"He made a nice career for himself. He's rebranded from, like, the Harvard smart quarterback, which never really made sense because if you watched him play, he looked like he might not be able to add. He was just crazy reckless. He was talented, but crazy reckless. And now, just because he has a long beard and we see his chest hair, he's charismatic? I don't get it."

Nick Wright isn’t feeling Ryan Fitzpatrick’s antics on TNF: “Just because he has a long beard and we see his chest hair, he’s charismatic? I don’t get it.” pic.twitter.com/NMHYAoEkpE

— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) September 18, 2026

When Wright questioned why FTF would even play the clip, anchor Kevin Wildes said it was a cool moment for Fitzpatrick to set off the tradition at the new stadium.

"Everybody does that in Buffalo. Literally everybody does it," Wright responded. "We don't typically promote other networks' pregame shows, and if we're gonna do it, let's pick a good one."

In typical Wright fashion, he offered this barb with a chuckle and a smile. But you could hear the old radio host coming out of him; somewhere not too deep down, Wright clearly thinks Fitzpatrick is way too beloved.

These were not the only shots Wright fired on Friday's First Things First. Wright also joked about the supposed new rules of consumption on live television after ESPN viewers caught a glimpse of Pat McAfee seemingly smoking weed.

title: Juan Soto's three-run shot lifts Mets to 6-3 win over Phillies
description: Juan Soto's three-run homer lifted the Mets to a 6-3 win in their home series opener against the Philadelphia Phillies on Friday night.
fullText:
The Mets (70-84) defeated the Philadelphia Phillies (85-69) by a score of 6-3.

-- Mets left-handed starter Zac Thornton plunked leadoff batter Kyle Schwarber on a 3-2 count to get the game started. The rookie battled back, striking out Trea Turner and Bryce Harper before Mets first baseman Brett Baty made a diving stop on a Luis Arraez grounder down the line to put away the third out.

-- Southpaw Tim Mayza served as the bullpen opener for Philadelphia, and Francisco Lindor jumped all over him with a leadoff double. With one out, Bo Bichette worked a 10-pitch at-bat, culminating in a single to center field which moved Lindor up to third base. Carson Benge kept the line moving and drove in Lindor with an opposite-field single. Mark Vientos was walked to load the bases, and Phillies manager Don Mattingly pulled Mayza for right-handed reliever Jose Urquidy. A.J. Ewing roped an Urquidy fastball for a double, which scored two runs. Urquidy retired the next two Mets batters to limit the damage to three runs.

-- In the second inning, Ewing got turned around on a deep line drive to center, failing to haul in the RBI double for Bryson Stott, which cut the Mets' lead to 3-1. In the bottom half of the inning, Juan Soto doubled into the left-center field gap with two outs, but Urquidy struck out Bichette to end the threat.

-- With two outs away in the top of the sixth, Phillies left fielder Edmundo Sosa blasted a solo shot to left field, his third hit of the night. Excluding Sosa, Thornton allowed just two hits. He struck out four and walked one, allowing two earned runs across 87 pitches.

-- Soto took a hanging breaking ball thrown by Phillies right-hander Orion Kerkering 428 feet for a two-out three-run homer in the bottom of the sixth. Soto's 26th tater of 2026 put the Mets up 6-2.

-- Philadelphia center fielder Derek Hill responded with a solo home run off of Mets left-handed reliever Nate Lavender in the top of the seventh. Lavender persevered, retiring each of the next four batters he faced, before handing the ball to Dedniel Núñez to record the third out of the eighth. In the bottom half of the frame, Bichette grounded into a double play with the bases loaded. Núñez handled the ninth inning and retired the side to earn the first save of his season - and second save of his career - to seal the 6-3 win for the Mets.

Soto notched his third game with multiple extra-base hits in September, going 3-for-5 with a double and a three-run homer. It was also Soto's third game of the season with at least three hits.

title: Angels notebook: Schanuel done for the year, good news on Natera and Ducks night
description: Nolan Schanuel's season is over due to his intercostal injury not getting any better, Samy Natera Jr. gets good news on an MRI and the Anaheim Ducks take a visit to the Big A.
fullText:
ANAHEIM, Calif. — Just as Nolan Schanuel's season started to take form, it was taken from him.

After a calf injury plagued the beginning of his season, Schanuel took off once he finally healed. A summer heater brought his numbers up to a .276 average with a .736 OPS, but that is where the progress will stop for this season.

Angels manager Kurt Suzuki said before Friday night's game that Schanuel isn't expected to return from his right intercostal muscle strain after having a set back during his rehab assignment.

"Just went on a rehab assignment and it wasn't feeling any better," Schanuel said. "Came back and talked to (head athletic trainer Mike Frostad) and the training staff, and they just thought it was best to take it easy and get back to being healthy."

Schanuel originally landed on the injured list on August 21 and began his rehab assignment in Triple-A Salt Lake on Sunday, but was scratched from his game on Wednesday. He said he felt something right away in the first inning of his last rehab assignment game, and it bothered him doing any baseball activity. After taking a day to try and let it go away, the irritation lingered and he came back to Anaheim to talk to the Angels' training staff to figure out the next steps.

He finishes his season hitting .301 with a .789 OPS in his final 50 games played.

"He started the year a little slower, battled some injuries, some nagging stuff," Suzuki said. "Once he got healthy, that's when you saw him take off. I mean, it was line drive after line drive. It was pretty impressive."

Although it's still lingering, Schanuel isn't concerned about this injury impacting his offseason. With the injuries and the hot stretch to end his season, Schanuel said he's learned a lot about himself this season, and knows what he needs to work on this winter.

"I think just understanding that I can be a really good contact bat in the lineup," Schanuel said. "Hit for a high average, get on base and power will come. I think if my power shows in doubles, then that's the kind of hitter I have to be.

The good news... Left-hander Samy Natera Jr.'s MRI results came back clean with no damage. He avoids any surgery and is on track for a normal offseason. He is still talking with the training staff about next steps, but he said it looks like six weeks of rehab and then build up arm strength like a normal offseason.

The bad news... the Angels placed Kyren Paris on the 10-day injured list with a right index finger fracture retroactive to September 15. Paris said he injured his finger fielding ground balls before Thursday's game and is expected to be out for three to four weeks. It ends his season, but he will have a normal offseason.

Friday is also Ducks night at Angel Stadium, which is an annual event where members of the Anaheim Ducks come out to the game, hit batting practice before the game and throw out the first pitch as the team gets ready to begin training camp.

Leo Carlsson, Cutter Gauthier, Beckett Sennecke, Tim Washe and Sam Colangelo were this year's batting practice participants from the Ducks, with A.J. Greer and Nick Jensen also hanging out.

As each player took swings, they began to realize baseball is harder than it may look.

"It's tough," Gauthier said. "It's far. It's a lot farther in person than it is over the TV."

"It's hard," Sennecke said. "It looks close, but it's farther than it looks."

Colangelo was one of the few that put together some quality swings. He grew up in Boston a massive Red Sox fan, and he played baseball until he was 12 years old.

Gauthier was another player that flirted with hitting a home run, but a couple of them fell short onto the warning track.

Carlssson and Gauthier are tabbed with throwing out the ceremonial first pitch before the game. Carlsson, however, has never thrown a baseball in his life.

He said he went to Dicks Sporting Goods on Thursday to buy a baseball "just to feel one for once."

"I just want to get it there," Carlsson said. "If it goes over, left, right, I don't care. I just gotta not skip one."

title: Darian Mensah turns in perfect first half for Miami with 20 completions on 20 attempts
description: Darian Mensah continued his impressive season with a perfect first half against Wake Forest on Sept. 18.
fullText:
It should come as a surprise to no one that Miami football is excellent this season. However, thanks to a schedule with all of the choppiness of a pond in July and three straight non-Saturday games, the Hurricanes have been very easy to overlook to date.

Darian Mensah did his part to get noticed Sept. 18. In the first half against Wake Forest, a conference opponent, Mensah completed 20 passes on as many attempts, breaking the Miami and ACC records for most consecutive completions in one game. He has 31 consecutive completions dating back to last week, also a Miami record, breaking Carson Beck's previous record of 24.

REQUIRED READING: College football Week 3 picks: Expert predictions, odds for every Top 25 game

Against Wake Forest, the Mensah-led Hurricanes jumped out to a 24-7 lead at halftime behind Mensah's 193 yards and two touchdowns.

It's just another day at the office for Mensah. He had a 93.8% completion percentage for the season at halftime, having completed 61-of-65 through two-and-a-half games. He also has 10 touchdowns and no interceptions thus far.

Former Western Carolina QB Taron Dickens might be sweating a bit watching Mensah. He's barely had a chance to enjoy his NCAA record of 50 straight completions, which he set last season. Dickens, who is now with Northern Illinois, went 53-of-56 in a game last year and started 46-of-46.

The FBS record belongs to Dominique Davis with 36; he completed 26 straight passes to open against Navy in 2011 for East Carolina.

Mensah is the Heisman Trophy favorite heading into Week 3, sitting at +400, ahead of the likes of Jeremiah Smith, teammate Malachi Toney, and Notre Dame QB CJ Carr.

Miami will have Nov. 7 circled on its calendar, as that's when it plays Notre Dame. Before that, ACC foes like Clemson and Florida State provide some of the tougher tests on the schedule, though they've also struggled mightily this year.

title: ‘I don’t really care’ – Kyle Larson speaks on how he feels about outside noise after winning or losing a race

fullText:
After breaking his streak of 51 races without a Cup Series win, Kyle Larson has spoken about how he feels about outside noise as a driver.

The Hendrick Motorsport driver's terrific win last week helped him not only end his long streak, but also put him only nine points behind Denny Hamlin, who currently holds the first position.

With eight more races to go, it has certainly opened things up for him, and the other NASCAR drivers who are in pursuit of winning the championship.

Denny Hamlin is the driver who Larson is currently trailing, but with a special night in Bristol, he could also get the job done.

Ahead of the crucial race on Sunday, Larson was asked about the 'Kyle Larson is good again' posters, and the two-time Cup Series champion has a solid response.

"I feel like I've raced long enough that I've seen it go like that," Larson said.

"When you win, you've got all these fans that jump on and are like 'See!? I told you he's good!' and this and that. And then I could literally go out there and do something stupid today or tomorrow and it completely flips like 'No, he sucks' and all that."

"I don't read too much into it, I don't let it get to my head either way. I don't really care what the outside noise is, whether it's good or bad, anymore.

"I just kind of focus on myself and my process, and our team and our process. And I think that's the key to being successful.

Larson and Hamlin were engaged in a close battle to win the championship last season. On that occasion, the format was different.

In this Chase Format, every race matters. A dip in form, which many believe Larson was experiencing, could have affected his bid for a title.

However, he has been solid since the start of the Chase, and the hope will be that Larson secures the championship.

title: Kirb Herbstreit offers flimsy defense for ESPN's decision to interview Ted Cruz on College GameDay
description: ESPN committed a bizarre broadcasting faux pas last Saturday, by giving Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) an extended platform on College GameDay to push for the passage of the so-called Protect College Sports Act (which also could be called the Screw College Players Act or, as Simms suggested, Protect the ESPN and SEC Contract Act).
fullText:
ESPN committed a bizarre broadcasting faux pas last Saturday, by giving Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) an extended platform on College GameDay to push for the passage of the so-called Protect College Sports Act (which also could be called the Screw College Players Act or, as Simms suggested, Protect the ESPN and SEC Contract Act). The story has resonated throughout the week, and it looms over Saturday's episode of College GameDay in Oxford, Mississippi.

Kirk Herbstreit, one of the College GameDay analysts, addressed the situation in comments with reporters on Friday.

"I was first really impressed," Herbstreit said, via Mississippi Today. "I've never seen a guy booed that long and be able to just power through that. You know, I don't know if he could hear what I could hear, but it was pretty — I think he was booed pretty much the entire time he spoke.

"I don't really get into politics. It's just not — I'm kind of an independent guy, right down the middle of the fairway. I'm for America, so whoever helps us as a country, I'm for. Whether it's somebody on the left, somebody on the right, so I don't really follow it. I don't know anything about his political views. I don't know what he's for or against. I care about football, my family, and my faith, and my country. Those are things I love.

"And so, I don't really pick sides, and I was surprised. I didn't know what his deal was, so him being booed, I asked people, 'Like, what's going on here?' And we had him on because they were gonna be voting this week, and maybe he could give us some insight to what's going on. That was really it. So we're not picking sides in any way at all. We just want to see the chaos that's surrounding this sport kind of be reeled in, and if this will help us get to that, then great. Now, the fact that the guy that sits right next to me, Nick Saban, was heavily involved in putting this act together, this guy loves college football more than anybody I've ever met. And so if he's happy about what this could do, then I follow his lead. But yeah, that was surprising. But, again, I don't really follow it, so I didn't really understand it."

There's a lot to unpack there. I'll keep it simple. Herbstreit is either flat-out lying or he's ridiculously naive.

How can anyone say "I love my country" while being completely detached from the issues that shape its present and future? How can any American adult not know what it means to be a Republican or to be a Democrat, and how those labels have become so inherently polarizing and conducive to negative reactions?

Beyond Herbstreit's claim that he's clueless as to why someone like Ted Cruz would be booed, Herbstreit's position that he's "right down the middle of the fairway" and that ESPN isn't "picking sides" on the issue at hand can't be reconciled with his viewpoint that the "chaos" needs to "kind of be reeled in" and that he supports anything Nick Saban recommends on the matter because Saban "loves college football more than anybody I've met."

It's entirely possible to love college football and to want to limit player pay and mobility. Which is precisely what the Screw College Players Act will do.

The word "chaos" is a matter of perspective. From the players' perspective, it's not chaotic; they have real rights and power. From the perspective of those who don't like the fact that the rabbit has the gun, it's definitely chaotic. Because the rabbit has the gun.

The best news is that folks seem to be figuring out what's going on here. The powers-that-be don't like the fact that they've lost some of their power, given the implosion of a system that was fueled by antitrust violations that collectively prevented players from getting paid. In the aftermath of the reckoning, those who don't like the new reality are shedding crocodile tears and screaming "the sky is falling" to anyone who may be able to help them implement a system that limits the new rights the players enjoy.

It's a grift. It's a scam. Herbstreit has made himself part of that scam while pretending to be neutral — and not even his dog will shield him from the criticism he now deserves.

description: The Royals started hot, but finished with a dud.
fullText:
The game started off so well for the Royals as they got out to a 4-0 lead after the top of the third. But the Pirates scored 8 over the remaining six offensive innings, and the Royals could only score 1 more. KC, therefore, fell to Pittsburgh by a score of 8-5.

Paul Skenes, in his first career start against KC, began well against the Royals. He struck out Carter Jensen and got Bobby Witt Jr. on a routine lineout to center. However, Vinnie Pasquantino was not intimidated by Skenes' ace bona fides.

In the top of the third, the Royals struck again. Kyle Isbel got a one-out single up the middle, then Bobby lined a single to right. Vinnie came through again, this time with an RBI single. Maikel Garcia then got his first hit since returning from the IL earlier this week, a double into right field. Maikel was thrown out trying to stretch it into a triple, but not before Vinnie scored the third run of the inning and gave the Royals what seemed like a reasonable lead.

On the other side, it was clear Randy Dobnak was not going to have his best night, despite getting to pitch in front of friends and family as the stadium is only a few miles from where he grew up. He danced around trouble in the first two innings but gave up a two-run bomb to Brandon Lowe in the bottom of the third. Michael Massey got one of those back in the top of the fourth.

Your browser does not support the video tag. Download the video.

However, Dobnak's struggles continued in the bottom of the fourth inning. He ultimately gave up two more runs before being relieved by Connor Thomas, with Lowe coming back to the plate. Thomas retired Lowe with a strikeout, and the Royals clung to a 5-4 lead. Still, they'd been hitting Skenes hard all night. Surely they could get some more, right?

Nate Pearson, likely the Royals' best current reliever, was tasked with pitching the seventh inning. Since coming to KC, Nate* had compiled a 1.57 ERA and 0.5 fWAR. Most on the team by anyone pitching in relief, except for Daniel Lynch IV. After giving up three runs tonight, unfortunately, that ERA rises to 2.63. Still good, but considerably higher. Pearson has now allowed at least one run in three straight appearances. He was battling his control in this one; he walked 1, hit another, and allowed 3 hits. He did strike out 2, but it just wasn't enough.

*He really needs a good reliever nickname; anyone got any ideas? I've got bupkis so far.

On the bright side, Anthony Gose continues to make a case for a bullpen spot next year. I wasn't sold even a week ago, but now he's struck out 4 over 2 innings in his last 3 appearances. He has also given up 3 hits, so let's not ink him to a multi-year deal, just yet, but there is some promise there. And, even better, Lucas Erceg was tasked with pitching the eighth.

We all know Erceg's story, and I think most of us are hoping for the best for him. He impressed a lot of people in his first appearance back against Houston, but I wasn't sure I was among them when I watched the replay. Watching live tonight, I'm sold. Pitching like this, he is going to mow some batters down. Sure, he didn't strike anyone out, and he allowed a hit. But the hit was allowed after a filthy front-hip sinker was called a ball, making the count 2-0. Things probably go very differently if it's a 1-1 count after that pitch. For that matter, Bryan Reynolds is credited with a double, and I can't say he didn't hit it hard, but I will say he was behind that pitch. If he'd been more on time, it's probably an out because the Royals were playing him to pull. He was tunneling the sinker and slider with elite effectiveness, and none of the remaining three batters made particularly good contact. In fact, the inning-ending double play might have been in doubt if Ryan O'Hearn were a faster runner because it was hit so softly.

More important than whether the Royals won or lost this game are the things that can help them plan their roster for next year. The return of an unfair Lucas Erceg would be a huge boon for next year's team.

The Royals will take another shot at the Pirates tomorrow evening; Noah Cameron (3.84 ERA, 4.13 SIERA) will face Bubba Chandler (4.28 ERA, 4.78 SIERA) at 5:40 PM Central Time. It should be a really fun pitching matchup.

title: Dave Roberts Reveals Dodgers’ Plan for Blake Snell After Groin Injury
description: The Dodgers are "optimistic" that they avoided the "hopeful" that starter Blake Snell will make another start in the regular season.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are "optimistic" that they avoided the "hopeful" that starter Blake Snell will make another start before the end of the regular season.

Snell left Wednesday's game early with groin tightness, pitching just one inning. After the game, the southpaw told the media the decision to exit was more precautionary than anything else.

After checking in with Snell on Thursday and Friday following his start, the Dodgers manager believes Snell will start at some point in the remaining eight games after Friday.

As for the nature of his pitching appearance, Roberts expects a normal workload, possibly pulling the plug a bit early out of precaution, but mindful that Snell would benefit from the running.

"I think it'd be more of a normal start, maybe not pushing him a ton, given we don't know how the season's going to play out," Roberts said on Friday, September 18th, before the game.

"But this will be his last regular season start, so I think it'd be more of a regular start."

Naturally, Roberts was asked whether it would be best to avoid having him pitch at all, out of caution.

The skipper explained that, given the nature of a possible bye and so many days off, there are downsides to letting him go cold.

"There is a thought, but you're still talking about a potential 17 days [in between starts]," Roberts explained.

"That's a long time to not be in competition, where typically, with his history, you still have rehabs and things like that.

"So it's not just plug-and-play: sit it out for two weeks and pitch in a playoff game."

Given Snell's history of groin-related injuries, the Dodgers would be wise to proceed cautiously, but their willingness to feel good about him starting should inspire confidence.

The real test will be how he goes day by day, as the Dodgers still have time to change course.

title: Kylian Mbappe’s On deal shows why endorsements are no longer enough
description: Kylian Mbappe did not leave Nike because he needed another company to supply his boots. After nearly 20 years with one of sportswear’s biggest brands, the Real Madrid striker already understood what a traditional endorsement partnership could offer. His agreement with On promises something different. Mbappe received an ownership stake in the Swiss […] The post Kylian Mbappe’s On deal shows why endorsements are no longer enough appeared first on ClutchPoints.
fullText:
Kylian Mbappe's On deal shows why endorsements are no longer enough appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

Kylian Mbappe did not leave Nike because he needed another company to supply his boots. After nearly 20 years with one of sportswear's biggest brands, the Real Madrid striker already understood what a traditional endorsement partnership could offer.

His agreement with On promises something different.

Mbappe received an ownership stake in the Swiss company, according to The Athletic. He will also contribute to the creation and testing of On's football products as the brand prepares to enter a market dominated by Nike, Adidas and Puma.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The financial details remain private, but the structure reveals why the partnership appealed to him. On did not recruit Mbappe simply to wear its logo. It invited him to help build an entire football operation.

"From the beginning, what drew me to On was the opportunity to build something entirely new together that will help shape tomorrow's game," Mbappe said in a statement, per ESPN.

That opportunity makes the agreement more compelling than another lucrative sponsorship. Mbappe can now connect his financial interests, playing experience and worldwide profile to the development of a new brand.

Nike began sponsoring Mbappe in 2006, when he was only nine. The partnership followed him from childhood into the highest level of football, where Nike placed him alongside Cristiano Ronaldo and Erling Haaland as one of its most important players.

Nike recognized that history after Mbappe decided to leave.

"Kylian's journey with Nike began when he was nine years old," the company told The Athletic. "Over nearly two decades, we've shared moments that shaped the game."

That statement captures what Mbappe walked away from. Nike offered familiarity, prestige and a relationship that covered most of his life. On offered the chance to create something with his name attached to its foundation.

Mbappe made that distinction clear while explaining his decision.

"I want to bring my experience and perspective into what we create, push what's possible through innovation, and always stay true to the joy of football," he said. "We have a shared dream, and this is only the beginning."

The word "create" matters. Traditional endorsement deals often position athletes as the final piece of a campaign. A company designs the product, constructs the message and then uses a famous face to sell both.

On wants Mbappe involved earlier in that process. He can provide feedback during product development, test the company's football footwear and help determine how the brand presents itself within the sport.

The equity component adds another layer. Mbappe will not merely collect compensation for representing On. He now owns a piece of the company whose football ambitions will depend heavily on his involvement.

On founder and co-CEO David Allemann does not want the company to imitate the brands that already control much of the football market.

"Football doesn't need another sportswear brand to do more of the same," Allemann said. "Football needs new ideas and a challenge to what is possible."

That approach explains why On targeted Mbappe. A company cannot credibly market itself as a fresh alternative while treating its leading athlete exactly like every established brand does. Giving Mbappe equity and direct access to product development supports the identity On wants to create.

The company has followed a similar strategy in tennis. Roger Federer joined On as an investor in 2019, while Iga Swiatek and Ben Shelton became prominent representatives of its relatively small roster.

Shelton previously explained why that structure appealed to him.

"I didn't want to be one of 50 Nike guys," he said in 2024.

Mbappe held a much bigger role at Nike than Shelton did, but the central attraction still applies. On can offer personal attention that becomes harder to guarantee within a deep roster of global stars.

Thierry Henry also strengthened the pitch. The former France and Arsenal striker has quietly worked as On's director of football since 2025 and helped convince Mbappe to join after his Nike contract expired.

"Building something new in football requires a bold and original approach," Henry said. "We want to listen to players, understand what they need and create something that can genuinely add to the game."

Henry's presence gives Mbappe another former elite player with whom he can communicate throughout the process. It also supports On's promise that athletes will influence the products rather than appear only after development ends.

On plans to make its premium football boots available to consumers in 2027, although Mbappe could wear his new footwear on the field within weeks. Barcelona and Switzerland player Sydney Schertenleib will also assist with development after expanding her existing partnership with the company.

"I've already experienced how differently On thinks about performance and design," Schertenleib said, adding that she had "never felt the ball" as she did while testing the company's product.

The boots still must prove themselves once players and consumers can judge them. Signing Mbappe alone will not guarantee that On can challenge companies with far more experience in football.

However, On has already given people a reason to pay attention. Mbappe could have moved from Nike to another familiar sportswear giant. Instead, he chose a company making its first push into football because it offered him influence and ownership.

That choice reflects a broader truth about modern athlete partnerships. Exposure matters, and guaranteed money always will. However, the most powerful athletes can now ask for more than a campaign, a signature product or a check.

They can ask for a seat at the table.

Mbappe spent nearly two decades helping Nike sell its vision. With On, he has an opportunity to help shape the vision itself and benefit if it succeeds.

For a player who already has worldwide recognition, that may hold more value than another endorsement ever could.

title: José Ramírez homers, reaches 1,000 RBIs as Guardians down A's 5-3 to stay atop AL Central

fullText:
CLEVELAND (AP) — José Ramírez and rookie Travis Bazzana homered and Joey Cantillo pitched six scoreless innings as the Cleveland Guardians rallied to beat the Athletics 5-3 on Friday night and stay atop the AL Central.

Ramírez connected in the sixth inning to give the Guardians a two-run cushion. His 12th homer was also the seven-time All-Star's 1,000th RBI, making him just the second Cleveland player to reach the plateau. Earl Averill drove in 1,084 runs.

Bazzana snapped a 3-3 tie in the fifth as the Guardians came back after falling behind 3-0 in the first.

Cleveland, 18-9 since Aug. 20, came in tied with Chicago for first in the division. The White Sox hold the head-to-head tiebreaker.

Cantillo (10-9) allowed two hits in six innings after replacing opener Daniel Espino. Cantillo has not given up a run in 10 innings over his past two outings.

Hunter Gaddis and Cade Smith finished off the combined three-hitter. Smith worked the ninth for his 38th save.

Zack Gelof hit a three-run homer for the A's, who are 0-4 on their final road trip of 2026.

Bazzana put Cleveland ahead 4-3 in the fifth with his 15th homer, a 411-foot leadoff drive to center off Scott Blewett (2-1).

The Guardians had squandered early scoring chances, loading the bases in the first two innings but failing to push a run across.

Cleveland finally strung some hits together in the fourth, scoring three times off starter Mason Barnett to tie it.

Rocchio, who leads all MLB No. 9 hitters in RBI with 50, delivered a two-run double and scored on Ramírez's two-out single.

Espino opened for Cleveland and started poorly.

The right-hander walked three in the first and allowed the three-run homer to Gelof, his 19th.

LHP Jacob Lopez (6-4, 5.02 ERA) starts Saturday for Oakland against Tanner Bibee (6-15, 4.16), who has gotten minimal support (3.05 runs per game) this season.

title: What Was RV Marquette’s Plan Against #9 Georgetown?
description: The Golden Eagles gave up an early goal and never mounted much of an attempt at a comeback.
fullText:
Okay, look, I get why Marquette men's soccer may have wanted to try to goofball their way to a scoreless draw against #9 Georgetown on Friday night. MU scored just five goals in Big East play last year while going 1-7-0, and trying to muck up the conference opener on the road against a top 10 ranked team honestly seems like a decent plan.

However, Matthew Van Horn scored for the home team in the 17th minute, on what was Georgetown's third shot of the match. That margin held to halftime, and Marquette got outshot 8-0 through the first 45 minutes, 5-0 after Van Horn's goal. Again, I get it if the original plan was "drag Georgetown to hell," but once you're down 1-0 early, you have to have a second plan. It didn't seem like Marquette had a second plan.

Marquette's first shot of the match didn't come until the 68th minute. Georgetown went up 2-0 in the 73rd, and then 3-0 in the 78th, which ended up as the final margin. Marquette's second shot was in the 74th, and they tacked on two more attempts in the 81st and 87th.

Four shots, all after trailing 1-0, all after halftime, three after trailing 2-0, two after trailing 3-0.

Oh, and by the way? Tomiwa Adewumi? He of the 22 minute hat trick last time out? Eight goals on nine shots on goal this season? Sat on the bench for the first 23 minutes of the second half and ended up not recording a shot.

What was the plan here, exactly? Certainly doesn't feel like there was a plan to actually win the game, much less actually rummage up a positive result. Feels like a very disappointing way to celebrate the appearance of a couple of votes in the United Soccer Coaches poll, y'know?

Up Next: Because scheduling is weird, Marquette will take a break from Big East play for a midweek contest coming up on Tuesday night. title: 5 things to watch in 49ers' home opener vs. Dolphins
description: Five things to watch as the San Francisco 49ers try to get to 2-0.
fullText:
The San Francisco 49ers face the Miami Dolphins in Week 2 back at their home site, Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, California, following their season opener in Melbourne, Australia.

The Niners are all smiles, feeling good after many days of rest coming off their 15,812-mile roundtrip. They opened the season with a dominant win against the Los Angeles Rams, 27-7, completely dismantling their NFC West rivals.

San Francisco proved it has multiple offensive weapons for quarterback Brock Purdy to choose from. He went 25-of-34 for 205 yards and three touchdowns. His connection with veteran receiver Mike Evans was displayed and he reunited with Deebo Samuel Sr. The 49ers saw a snippet of how good the running back tandem of Christian McCaffrey and rookie Kaelon Black can be. And San Francisco's defense showed signs it could be one of the best in the league.

However, a familiar sight was also seen for the 49ers: injuries. They suffered two blows, losing De'Zhaun Stribling and Jake Tonges in their win against the Rams. Stribling is out for 10 weeks with an ankle injury, per head coach Kyle Shanahan, while Tonges is out for the year with an MCL injury in his knee.

Still, the 49ers are confident in their positional depth. It's "next man up" again, something they're accustomed to.

Here are five things to look for in the San Francisco 49ers' home opener vs. the Miami Dolphins:

The 49ers set the tone against the Rams behind a near-perfect performance from quarterback Brock Purdy, who finished with a 105.6 rating with 205 yards, three touchdowns and an interception. In order for San Francisco to get a win streak going, it is going to need Purdy to be Purdy. The calm, the relief for San Francisco.

Four years ago, Purdy made his NFL debut against the Dolphins after Jimmy Garoppolo was injured.

"I think I've talked about it a lot just over the years, because it was such an impressive game. We had such a good team that year and it's such mixed feelings when you lose your starter and your backup within a month of each other," head coach Kyle Shanahan recalled to reporters. "Then you're down to the third-string quarterback the whole game. So, it was a little sombering after the game and stuff, but I remember always talking about, when I got home that night and actually sitting and thinking about the game and really setting in how well Brock played."

Purdy stepped into that 2022 game in the first quarter and completed 25 of 37 pass attempts for 210 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in the Niners' 33-17 win.

"Just going against that defense he did under duress with all the blitzes, how he hung in there, took hits, how he didn't get many reps at all the whole year and how he knew exactly where to go with the ball," Shanahan said. "It was just one game, but it was an extremely special game. It was foreshadowing how the following three years would go after that game."

It was a near-perfect game, especially coming from the third-string QB. Now, Purdy is the man and provides that sense of security for the Niners. He doesn't make many mistakes. When Purdy is perfect, or close to it, good things happen for San Francisco.

Sometimes, an offense is only as good as the offensive line. The Niners' was as good as ever against the Rams, which included limiting reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett. The combination of Trent Williams, Connor Colby, Jake Brendel, Dominick Puni and Colton McKivitz did not allow any sacks on Purdy against LA in Australia. As for the run blocking, both McCaffrey and Black each racked up at least 65 rushing yards.

The effort was recognized and will need to be replicated against the Dolphins.

"I thought they were unbelievable," Shanahan said of the offensive line. "The pass protection especially, just a huge challenge going against that team and the way they were all tied together as a unit. A lot of good individual plays, but just how they did as a group throughout the whole game was really impressive. And they run-blocked very well too."

Expect a similar performance from San Francisco's front line against Miami, which is coming off a 27-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders where they allowed 290 total yards, including 130 rushing yards.

This emerging tandem has been one of the sleeper wins for San Francisco. As dynamic as McCaffrey is, the 49ers want to ensure that he's available to play meaningful football late in the season and into the playoffs. It was evident how helpful it was to McCaffrey to have Black as the No. 2 running back.

Out the backfield, the two combined for 133 yards on 24 carries. McCaffrey averaged 6.8 per carry on 10 attempts, while Black averaged 4.8 on 14.

"Yeah, it did work out," Shanahan said of his backfield tandem. "I was a little surprised at the end just that Kaelon got more than Christian. That was just kind of how the game went. Has a lot to do with probably me starting out the game. I think I had like three runs in the first 17 plays, but love taking some off Christian and love the fact that Kaelon was prepared for everything, the run game and the pass game, and allowed us to be able to do that."

The better Black can be, the more he's trusted to be on the field. The more he's on the field, the more McCaffrey can save his body. An available McCaffrey makes the 49ers that much more dangerous.

Rookie receiver Stribling suffering an ankle injury that will keep him out for 10 weeks is a bummer. Backup tight end Tonges being out out for the season with an MCL injury hurts, too.

However, the good news for the 49ers is they have depth when it comes to offensive weapons to accommodate Purdy. Veteran receivers Evans and Samuel each had six catches and scored touchdowns against the Rams. Evans pulled in 49 yards, while Samuel's reunion ended with 48 yards. Demarcus Robinson was a downfield threat with two catches for 50 yards and a touchdown.

McCaffrey and Black can be targets for Purdy out of the backfield, but expect Luke Farrell to step up as the No. 2 tight end, behind George Kittle, with Tonges going down. Kittle is expected to be 100% against the Dolphins after being a full participant during the Niner's Friday practice.

This defensive core looks as good as any defensive unit in the NFL, led by Fred Warner, Dre Greenlaw and Nick Bosa. They have some surprising rookie standouts early on in linebacker Jaden Dugger and defensive lineman Gracen Halton.

The mastermind is defensive coordinator Raheem Morris.

"I thought he did a real good job just mixing up the fronts, the looks, the stunts, picking the right times when to pressure, some four-man, some five-man, but he mixed it up really well throughout the game," Shanahan said of Morris.

The 49ers limited the Rams offense to just one touchdown, forced two turnovers and the Rams had just a 22% third down efficiency rating. However, Morris isn't getting too high over one win.

"I think you got to stay even keel. I think you got to go through the process each and every week. We played a good game, played a good enough game to go out there and win," Morris said. "That was important. There's always going to be things you got to clean up. There's always going to be things you want to do better.

"But I'm really proud of how the group responded and how they went out and handled the adversity of the travel, handled the adversity of playing a very good football team that we played and going out there and getting a win."

He knows with De'Von Achane coming in, they are going to have to be disciplined and ready to go, play a physical brand of football and be ready to hit.

"Tough, fast. He gets mistaken that he's an outside runner, but he lowers his pads, he runs for the extra yards, he does the special things that we talk about in running where he makes five (yards), eight and he makes eight, 10. Then, if you're not careful, he can make a really explosive run or catch. Presents a lot of challenges for us," Morris said.

title: Serena Williams’ former coach responds to fans criticising Carlos Alcaraz for his reaction to US Open loss
description: A maiden Grand Slam title at the 2026 US Open looked like it was simply meant to be for Ben Shelton after his incredible triumph...
fullText:
A maiden Grand Slam title at the 2026 US Open looked like it was simply meant to be for Ben Shelton after his incredible triumph over Carlos Alcaraz in the quarterfinals.

In what marked the biggest win of his career thus far, Shelton defeated Alcaraz in a phenomenal five-set bout at Arthur Ashe Stadium, which lasted four hours and 28 minutes, finishing at 3:33 am New York time.

The Spaniard, defending his title at the US Open, had shocked many fans with his level in the first four rounds of the tournament.

Following four months on the sidelines with a wrist injury, Alcaraz dropped just one set en route to the quarterfinals and comfortably beat 20th seed Tommy Paul.

After the loss to Shelton, fans would have been forgiven for thinking the winner of the quarterfinal match was Alcaraz, who left the court with a beaming smile on his face.

Discussing Alcaraz's reaction to the loss, Serena Williams' former coach, Rick Macci, responded to the 23-year-old's critics.

In a post on X, Macci said: "Carlos being called out because he was smiling and saying how he was very happy after the 5 hour street fight with Shelton.

"He was being honest. Period. It was not fake. For others to throw knives at the Magician shows they lack real knowledge and are inexperienced of the mental makeup of not good or great, but a special generational talent.

"Sure, he did not play solid, but after not playing pure combat for 139 days and many doubts, worries and feelings about the wrist, the Spanish Magician was just so happy to be back in the mix and perform on stage with his gifts from above that we all smile and love."

Prior to the US Open, Alcaraz's last tournament appearance came at the Barcelona Open back in April.

He had planned to feature at the Cincinnati Open before heading to New York, but withdrew from the tune-up event to continue his recovery.

title: Washington football generating elite havoc rate on defense
description: The Washington Huskies have been among the nation's best at generating havoc plays on defense.
fullText:
Throughout fall camp, defensive coordinator Ryan Walters had one clear message when it came to improvements he wanted to see made on his defense: create more havoc plays. Just two weeks into the season, Washington's defense has wasted no time doing so. The Huskies are currently tied for No. 3 in the nation in turnover margin while ranking amongst the top teams in the country in havoc rate.

While the term "havoc rate" can be seen as a general statement to have an increased sense of intensity and urgency as a unit, there are analytics to back it up. The statistic refers to a defense's ability to create negative plays for opposing offenses, including tackles for loss, forced fumbles, pass breakups, and interceptions.

According to CFBTrack, the Huskies currently rank as the No. 4 defense in the country with a havoc rate of 27.8 percent, meaning they are creating a negative play approximately once in every four snaps. Washington trails only New Mexico, Virginia Tech, and LSU.

"We've been opportunistic for sure as a program," said Walters during Tuesday's press conference. "Not just as a staff, but as a program, we've definitely put an emphasis on generating takeaways and taking care of the football, so our offense has done a great job of not turning it over. So that's why were where were at, and we've taken advantage of opportunities to get takeaways, and so hopefully that trend continues throughout the course of the season."

One of the main contributors to the cause has been the defensive line, made up of a healthy rotation of veterans, transfers, and freshmen. On the interior, fourth-year Elinneus Davis has emerged as a leader in a group that features transfers Kai McClendon, DeSean Watts, and Darin Conley. That list doesn't include one of the most impactful new pieces of the line, freshman Derek Colman-Brusa, who has recorded 7 tackles, 2 for loss, and a sack in his first two games.

On the outside, starting edge rushers Jacob Lane and Ramzak Fruean have been a force to be reckoned with, but they're not the only ones wreaking havoc in the backfield. Fifth-year seniors Russell Davis II and Isaiah Ward, both of whom dealt with injury last year, have returned to play in a major way.

Davis tallied a sack in the Apple Cup, while Ward has recorded a tackle for loss to go along with a forced fumble and fumble recovery against Washington State. Now that both veteran Arizona transfers are healthy, Washington's pass rush has seen a massive leap in production from years past.

Him @AMcLaughlin28 ☔️ pic.twitter.com/3cEBh6YG9Y

To go along with a sturdy front seven is a secondary that flies to the ball, highlighted by safety Alex McLaughlin and freshman cornerback Jeron Jones. Through the first two weeks, the Huskies' back line has combined for five interceptions, with McLaughlin being responsible for a pair, Jones having one to his name, while Rahshawn Clark came up with the game-sealing pick against Utah State.

As Walters and his unit prepare for Eastern Washington ahead of Big Ten play, it will look to stay consistent in their ability to stifle opposition while creating extra possessions for an offense that has struggled so far.

fullText:
Immigrants applying to live permanently in the United States can be rejected if they receive public benefits, beginning this week.

Use of Medicaid, food stamps, tuition assistance and free school lunch programs, among other government assistance, could all be grounds for denying a green-card application.

The policy from President Donald Trump's administration, which took effect Friday, marks a dramatic change to a long-standing federal policy consistent with the president's efforts to restrict legal immigration pathways.

The rule could reduce federal and state payments by $13 billion a year, by persuading some 950,000 people to disenroll from or avoid federal safety net programs, according to estimates from the Department of Homeland Security. The agency said that the rule aligns with Congress's intent that noncitizens "in the United States be self-sufficient and not dependent on taxpayer-funded government benefits."

"Aliens in the United States should be self-reliant," a DHS policy document for the rule states, "and government benefits should not incentivize immigration."

Applying for a green card, or legal permanent residency, is a necessary step for those seeking U.S. citizenship.

This week, New York led 21 other states, the District of Columbia and several cities in suing the Trump administration over the new rule. The lawsuit argued that the rule fails "to consider many important aspects" of the problems it creates and warned that the harms will extend to mixed-status families and U.S. citizen children.

"Cruelty is the point," New York Attorney General Letitia James (D) said at a news conference announcing the lawsuit this week. "Having a chilling effect on immigrants is the point. Letting individuals know that they are not welcome here is the point."

The rule allows immigration officers to use their judgment in considering whether use of benefits such as food stamps indicates that a person is "likely at any time to become a public charge," or dependent on government assistance. Critics warn that an absence of clear guidance on which benefits will be considered in a green-card application will led to inconsistent application and a broader chilling effect.

"The lack of specificity makes it really hard for any family to know what [government-provided benefit] is safe to use," said Julia Gelatt, an associate director at the Migration Policy Institute, a nonpartisan think tank.

The Department of Homeland Security rule expands the "public charge" policy in place since 1882. Immigration officers have long factored in a person's health, finances and skills in determining whether they are likely to rely on government assistance in the future. But only direct cash payments, such as disability income, and long-term hospitalization, previously were considered reasons for denying a green-card application.

The new rule applies to immediate family members of U.S. citizens and legal permanent residents, including children and spouses, fiancés of U.S. citizens, skilled and religious workers, and others.

Other types of immigrants, including asylum seekers and refugees, will not be subject to the rule.

The first Trump administration introduced a similar rule in 2019 that was later blocked by courts. But the policy spread fear and confusion among immigrant households, leading to a sharp drop in people living in households where someone lacked a green card enrolling in noncash federal assistance programs, such as food stamps, according to an Urban Institute report.

title: U.S. military had close call after using AI to generate intelligence report
description:
US Army soldiers conduct unmanned aerial system training in April 2026. - Spc. Alva Gonzalez/US Army
The intelligence report, circulated across the US military this spring in the midst of the war with Iran, immediately set off alarm bells: A Chinese ship in the Middle East was transporting components of a nuclear weapons program.

fullText:
The intelligence report, circulated across the US military this spring in the midst of the war with Iran, immediately set off alarm bells: A Chinese ship in the Middle East was transporting components of a nuclear weapons program.

The US military swung into action with plans to intercept the vessel, according to four sources familiar with the episode. According to two of the sources, armed members of the US military were preparing to board the ship. Military planes were in the air, one of those sources and another source familiar with the incident said.

It was only just before the planned operation that officials dug deeper into the report put together by a special operations command analyst and found it had been generated with the help of artificial intelligence (AI) — and that a chatbot the analyst had used inaccurately identified the material the ship was carrying. CNN was not able to learn what the misidentified cargo was.

The report, according to one of the sources, was “entirely false.” But it also “almost started a war,” the source said. Any US operation against a Chinese vessel could have risked spiraling into an armed conflict between the two nations.

Across the US military and the intelligence community, officials are pushing to weave AI into nearly every facet of their work, from analyzing the huge volumes of raw intelligence the US collects and selecting targets for strikes, to more mundane applications like managing budgeting, logistics and supply chains.

But the episode underscores the profound risks of using this powerful, new and relatively poorly understood technology for targeting in the middle of a war. Analysts have long feared that AI could lead to a catastrophic miscalculation if nation states are relying on poor or corrupted data — the kind of miscalculation that might lead the United States to fire on a Chinese ship based on inaccurate information.

In this particular instance, the analyst queried a chatbot about some intelligence reporting on the ship’s manifest that originated with US Special Operations Command Pacific, based in Hawaii. It was not clear whether the chatbot was a commercially available one or a US government product.

“The internal tools are mostly just copies of the commercial stuff wearing lipstick,” a former senior US official familiar with the AI systems used by military and intelligence analysts.

The bot fused together open-source intelligence with secret signals intelligence in government holdings and reached its fateful conclusion about the material the ship was carrying.

The analyst then used AI again to package the findings into a standard intelligence report — the kind that is trusted by military officials — and disseminated it.

US Special Operations Command Pacific and the Pentagon did not respond to a request for comment.

The rationale for the rapid adoption of AI is that it can help the military make battlefield decisions, like which targets to strike or which military assets to move where, faster. Officials say the US can’t afford to fall behind in integrating AI in case it must one day fight China or another adversary who would potentially be able to stay one step ahead of the US.

In January, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth released his agency’s “Artificial Intelligence Acceleration Strategy” in a bid to speed up the military’s use of AI.

“We will unleash experimentation, eliminate bureaucratic barriers, focus our investments and demonstrate the execution approach needed to ensure we lead in military AI,” Hegseth said in a speech announcing the strategy.

The strategy also pushes for its broad use across the military, ordering the department to make AI available via several programs with the aim of “democratizing AI experimentation and transformation across the Department by putting America’s world-leading AI models directly in the hands of our three million civilian and military personnel, at all classification levels,” a memo announcing the strategy said.

But the effort is decentralized, multiple US officials familiar with the dynamic said, with different parts of the government using different tools under different orders and safety standards. There’s no one set of standards for how the US verifies the information generated by these tools. The constellation of different AI systems being deployed by disparate corners of the military and intelligence community means that the relative reliability and functionality vary widely.

For weeks, Washington policymakers have been intensely debating AI after a series of dire warnings from Silicon Valley engineers and tech CEOs of the possibility that AI could break free of human constraints, with potentially civilization-ending consequences.

But the episode with the Chinese ship underscores a different, and more immediate risk: human beings making disastrous decisions based on inaccurate or misleading information generated by AI or other automated systems. Sources said that the military is rapidly turning to AI to help with targeting, an area which holds the obvious risk of fatal mistakes.

“AI in targeting is definitely something that is ramping up and there is no real guidance for how having a human in the loop will prevent civilian casualties or fratricide,” another source familiar with the military’s current policies said.

The kind of “hallucination” that the tool used by the analyst in this case conjured has not been an isolated incident across the intelligence community since these tools began proliferating across government, according to one of the sources.

For some older intelligence officials — even those who broadly support the use of AI inside the military — AI has put pressure on analysts to produce and disseminate intelligence faster, opening the door for mistakes. Young analysts in particular, several sources said, are natives on these tools and more likely to trust them uncritically.

“AI allows you to get to a bad idea faster,” one of the sources said.

fullText:
WASHINGTON – Senate Republicans' three-month headache about Mitch McConnell's health seems to have subsided – at least for now.

In the days since the Kentucky lawmaker's return to the Capitol, they've defended him in the halls and expressed gratitude that his condition has improved. A fall in June, followed by a bout of pneumonia, kept the 84-year-old off the job for much of the summer and complicated the voting math for Senate Republicans on key legislation.

On his way back into the Senate chamber on the night of Monday, Sept. 14, he joked with reporters about admittedly dodging their questions since he'd been gone. Sitting in a wheelchair with visibly bruised hands, he resolved that it was "time to get back to work" and "finish the ​job for this Congress." He isn't running for reelection and will end his more than 40-year Senate tenure by January.

Sen. Thom Tillis, R-North Carolina, who's served in the Senate with McConnell for more than a decade and will also retire next year, said he had a "great conversation" with him on Thursday. It was "classic Mitch," Tillis told USA TODAY.

"I spent 20 seconds asking him how he's doing, and he goes right into preserving the filibuster, and who we have to look ahead to do it as we leave, and Ukraine," Tillis said.

McConnell has been a vocal proponent of maintaining U.S. military and diplomatic support for Ukraine amid its ongoing war with Russia, as well as shielding the filibuster, the 60-vote threshold in the Senate that he says encourages bipartisanship, from President Donald Trump's campaign to eliminate it.

His reemergence in the Capitol took the internet by storm. One moment in particular stood out: During a meeting of the Senate Agriculture Committee to vote on the farm bill, it appeared to some onlookers as though McConnell voted incorrectly, raising more questions about his mental state.

When McConnell voted yes, Sen. John Hoeven, R-North Dakota, leaned over and said something to him. But Hoeven told USA TODAY he wasn't correcting McConnell – he himself wasn't sure about whether they were taking a more procedural vote or voting on final passage of the bill out of committee.

"He voted, and he voted correctly," Hoeven said. "He was there. He was present. He got it right."

Hoeven and other Senate Republicans said they were happy to have McConnell back. The Senate will be in session for another two weeks before going on recess for more than a month until after the midterm elections in November.

"I haven't had a chance to run into him," Rand Paul, McConnell's Kentucky counterpart in the Senate, told USA TODAY. "But I'm glad he's back and glad he's doing better."

Zachary Schermele is the congressional correspondent for USA TODAY. Reach him by email at zschermele@usatoday.com and on Signal @zachschermele.02. Follow him on X at @ZachSchermele.

fullText:
President Donald Trump has announced an agreement with Greenland, in which the U.S. will take permanent control of the Arctic island’s security.

“I am pleased to announce that the United States of America has entered into an Agreement with The Kingdom of Denmark, and Greenland, that gives the United States permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland, completely addressing ALL of our many U.S. concerns,” Trump wrote on Truth Social Friday evening.

The president has eyed Greenland since before he returned to the White House in January 2025, arguing that the U.S. needed to control the semi-autonomous Danish territory for national security purposes.

Trump said that the agreement means the U.S. “will FOREVER have the complete ability to do what is necessary in Greenland in order to secure and defend the security of Greenland, and the United States of America.”

It’s unclear what exactly is in the agreement Trump claims to have struck with Denmark and Greenland, but he did highlight one major point — U.S. adversaries such as Russia and China will need his approval to work with Greenland militarily and economically.

“From now on, no U.S. adversary can EVER have a base in Greenland, have a military presence in Greenland, or make sensitive investments in Greenland, without our express written approval,” Trump said.

The president had warned Russia and China would take Greenland if he didn’t step in.

“It's so strategic. Right now, Greenland is covered with Russian and Chinese ships all over the place,” Trump claimed during a press gaggle aboard Air Force One in January. “We need Greenland from the standpoint of national security — and Denmark is not going to be able to do it.”

Trump boasted about his role in the new agreement with Greenland that he said would be “cherished by the American People.”

“For over 100 years, Presidents have known the strategic importance of Greenland, but NONE of them were able to do anything about it. I am proud to be the President that permanently and conclusively addressed this very important situation,” he wrote on Truth Social.

“We will immediately begin the process of developing a large Military presence in the appropriate part of Greenland, of which there are many. We will work with the people of Greenland in its development and construction,” he added.

Denmark’s prime minister, Mette Frederiksen, and the leader of Greenland’s government, Jens-Frederik Nielsen, released statements on Friday night saying that the agreement was expected to be signed at the UN General Assembly next week.

”It is encouraging that we are about to make an agreement that will ensure and strengthen the security of Greenland, the Kingdom of Denmark, the United States, and the Western Alliance. The agreement recognizes Greenland’s interests and our place in the international cooperation. It is to the benefit of us all,” said Nielsen.

Frederiksen added: ”I am glad that we are about to make a great agreement for Greenland, the Kingdom of Denmark, and the United States. An agreement which strengthens our common security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic Area and therefore is great for NATO and Europe as well. And an agreement which at the same time recognizes the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom and the Greenlandic people’s right to self-determination.”

Since Trump began pushing to acquire Greenland, he has been met with opposition, not just from the people of the Arctic island and Denmark, but also from America’s European allies.

“Greenland belongs to its people. It is for Denmark and Greenland, and them only, to decide on matters concerning Denmark and Greenland,” a joint statement from seven European leaders read.

In the January 6 statement, leaders from France, Germany, the United Kingdom and other U.S. allies said, “We and many other Allies have increased our presence, activities and investments, to keep the Arctic safe and to deter adversaries.”

They said that since Denmark is a part of NATO, “security in the Arctic must therefore be achieved collectively...by upholding the principles of the UN Charter, including sovereignty, territorial integrity and the inviolability of borders.”

Days later, Trump threatened to impose a 10 percent tariff on imports from European allies, several of which were part of the earlier joint statement, “until such time as a Deal is reached for the Complete and Total purchase of Greenland.”

Trump quickly backed down from his tariff threats, claiming to have “formed the framework of a future deal with respect to Greenland” with NATO chief Mark Rutte.

Even with the new agreement between government officials, it is doubtful that Trump will sway those in Greenland opposed to American intervention.

The day Trump threatened tariffs against European nations if he did not strike a deal to acquire Greenland, protesters in Nuuk held Greenlandic flags and a banner that read “Make America Go Away” and “We Are Not Property!”

“I think he should mind his own business,” Greenlander Lars Vintner, a heating engineer, told the Associated Press in January.

“What’s he going to do with Greenland? He speaks of Russians and Chinese and everything in Greenlandic waters or in our country,” he said. “Every summer we go sailing and we go hunting and I never saw Russian or Chinese ships here in Greenland.”

A majority of Americans are also not sold on the idea of gaining control of Greenland.

Fifty-eight percent of Americans oppose a U.S. takeover of the Arctic island while 21 percent favor it and 20 percent are unsure, according to a Pew Research Center poll from January.

CAIRO (AP) — Hundreds of thousands of Iranians rallied Friday in a government-organized show of defiance after months of war, pledging their readiness to take up arms in the biggest such demonstration since the United States and Israel attacked in February.

Iran's government has sought to rally the people and stress national unity, even as the economy worsens under a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports and new U.S. sanctions. On Friday, it claimed another attack on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway it has sought to control since the start of the war.

Estimates varied of the number of people volunteering to receive limited military training and defend the country in an effort described as "Janfaday-e Iran," or the "ones who sacrifice their lives for Iran." They marched through downtown Tehran in combat uniform, carrying flags, as onlookers cheered.

For days, state media have encouraged Iranians to join the campaign, saying training with assault rifles would begin soon. The volunteers would be an additional layer of security to the paramilitary Revolutionary Guard and the Basij militia, which has played a key role in quashing anti-government protests.

Tehran's Guard chief, Gen. Hassan Hassanzadeh, told the state broadcaster that over 600,000 people had registered to participate, with over 1 million expected to take part in the training. On Friday morning, the broadcaster estimated over 300,000 people were on the streets.

The new head of the Basij, Hossein Taeb, declared in a speech as the rally began that the volunteers will be ready for "full-fledged defense" and similar rallies will take place in other cities soon.

The new trainees will make a "nightmare" for Iran's enemies, Taeb added, as President Masoud Pezeshkian, military commanders and other senior officials watched the march.

Some participants trampled flags of the U.S. and Israel. Others chanted "Death to America" and "Death to Israel."

"I am here to tell (U.S. President Donald) Trump that we Iranians have no fear about his threats against our homeland," said Marzieh Afaghi, 24, who attended the rally with her toddler and husband. "No one in history could invade Iran and remain there."

The rally was also a chance for Iran to show off military hardware. Anti-aircraft batteries were on display, while female Guard members in black headscarves sat with truck-mounted machine guns.

The Guard displayed drones that have been used against ships in the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran's attacks and threats have severely affected the Gulf region's shipments of oil and natural gas to the rest of the world.

Iran said it had attacked a Togo-flagged oil tanker, the Trend, for what it called an "illegal attempt" to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, the state broadcaster reported. The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations center said a tanker was hit by a projectile, sparking a fire on board that was extinguished.

The UKMTO in a separate update said ship transits facilitated by the U.S. military off Oman have averaged 24 a day over the past week but overall traffic remains about 90% lower than before the war.

Friday's events also suggested that hard-liners like Taeb among Iran's leadership will be more prepared to suppress any future demonstration against the theocracy.

In January, shortly before the war, Iran saw some of its largest nationwide protests in history, which began over the struggling economy and turned to wider grievances. Activists have said a crackdown killed over 7,000 people and saw tens of thousands detained.

In May, government officials said more than 30 million people in Iran — which has a total population of some 90 million — had volunteered via an online form or at public gatherings to lay down their lives for the theocracy. The Associated Press could not independently confirm that.

Karimi reported from Tehran, Iran, and Anna from Jerusalem.

fullText:
Protesters are demanding Trump be removed as the Kennedy Center chairman.

Hundreds of activists gathered at the Kennedy Center Friday night in opposition to President Donald Trump's attempted takeover of the presidential memorial and threats that he will close and demolish it.

Activists linked hands and formed a human chain outside the Washington venue, demanding Trump be removed as its chairman for failing to protect and manage it. Trump installed himself as chairman of the Kennedy Center last year after removing its previous leadership and replacing board members with his own appointees.

"The demonstration opposes the recent sudden closure of the facility, the installation of security fencing, and political efforts to alter or demolish portions of the presidential memorial," the group said on its website.

The Hands Off the Arts organization behind the rally and protest said they expect hundreds of people to gather on the center's steps for musical performances, testimonials and speeches before forming a human chain around the building. The group has held various protests outside the performing arts venue this year.

"The Kennedy Center can't be renamed for anyone else. It's a memorial to John F. Kennedy. It's like silly to suggest otherwise. And it's not just silly -- it's insulting and it's degrading and it's un-American," Miller told ABC News.

Miller, who was a former assistant manager of dance programming at the Kennedy Center, lost her job in 2025 as part of mass layoffs as the administration restructured the Kennedy Center.

"Artists are the risk takers in our society," Miller said "... We are the people who create the world that comes next, and that is what the Kennedy Center means to all of us. This is a building that belongs to the American people, not one person and it's our Kennedy Center. We are the Kennedy Center."

The activist coalition, which says it formed after leadership changes at the Kennedy Center in recent months, said its goal is to reclaim the Kennedy Center from "authoritarian overreach and protect other arts and cultural institutions from similar fates," according to the group's website.

Earlier this week, Trump said the Kennedy Center could be "ripped down" if his administration doesn't receive recognition on the performing arts center as tensions over his name being removed from the venue mount.

"I think that the Trump administration should certainly have recognition. Because frankly, if we don't do that, it's going to close. It'll end up being ripped down," the president told reporters.

A federal judge on Thursday ordered the Kennedy Center to provide 30 days' notice before making any major physical changes to the building, including demolishing it as Trump has threatened.

U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper issued the order after lawyers for Democratic Rep. Joyce Beatty, an ex officio member of the board, cited Trump’s warning that the center could be "ripped down" and submitted photographs appearing to show the Trump examining a placard labeled "Kennedy Center DEMOLISHED" on Wednesday night. The photos were taken Wednesday night through a cabin window on Air Force One.

President Donald Trump is seen aboard Air Force One looking at a large printout of the Kennedy Center after landing at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland on September 16, 2026.

The venue "cannot install memorials for President Trump or anyone or anything else at the Kennedy Center without Congress’s blessing," Cooper ruled.

The judge earlier this week ruled that Trump's name could not be added to the center's exterior without congressional approval. The board previously placed his name on the facade, and removed it in June after an earlier ruling.

Trump has argued that the center is in poor condition and requires substantial government support to remain open.

"It's in very, very bad shape, very dangerous shape," Trump said Wednesday. "You see steel falling down. You see plaster falling off ceilings. You see a lot of dangers."

ABC News' Sarah Beth Hensley contributed to this report.
